audits.summary:
Today the Notices Dashboard is a faithful clone of a competitor's layout (Notice Alert) rather than a product designed around the firm's litigation workload: eight count-only tiles at 24px, a Company onboarding card and a mini calendar filling the left column, and a fixed 380x620px Notice Summary table on the right, everything set in 11px/10px text (23 sub-caption sizes, zero aria-labels, page root at space-y-2.5 against the enforced 8px/space-y-6 rhythm). The numbers a partner sees are not trustworthy: the extension's Sync All deletes and re-inserts every gst_notices row per client (extension/background.js:103-104), wiping staff_status/priority/assign_to/reply fields, which is why Open equals Total (1060/1060) and Replied is all dashes; "Last 24 Hours = 64" counts rows rewritten by the last sync, not new notices; "Over Due = 473" counts closed, replied and extended-due notices and, because due_date is parsed as UTC midnight, anything due today from 05:30 IST onward; PULL FAILED diagnostic rows are inserted into gst_notices and counted as notices. There is no list of actual notices on the page at all (no action queue), no owner, ageing, trend, or amount-at-stake view, even though the schema already holds due_date, extended_due_date, priority tiers, assign_to and amount_of_demand. The biggest lever is a two-part move: (1) fix the sync to an upsert that preserves staff columns and exclude sentinel rows, so the KPIs mean something; (2) rebuild the page around a "what needs attention today" queue rather than around counts.

TARGET LAYOUT (12-column grid, max-w none, gap-6, page root space-y-6; body text-sm, captions text-xs, numbers text-3xl tabular-nums; light-only semantic tokens): 
ROW 0 - PageHeader (full size, not embedded): title "Notices & Litigation", subtitle "Last portal sync 13 Sep 10:42 · 92 GSTINs · 3 failed logins" (from client_sync_log), actions right: [Sync All] (primary, with extension-state chip), [Add Notice], [Export]. Below it a filter bar (sticky at top of main): Financial Year, Client (searchable), Owner, Category, Status, Date range, plus the existing Registration/Other toggle; the top-nav pill group becomes an underline Tabs row (Overview | Notices | Submissions | Refunds | DRC-03 | Reports) with the active tab derived from useLocation.
ROW 1 (above the fold) - six KPI tiles in one row (col-span-2 each): Open notices; Overdue (destructive); Due in 7 days (warning); Unassigned (info); High priority; Demand under dispute (₹, from amount_of_demand). Each tile: label text-xs muted, value text-3xl, a 7-day delta caption ("+12 vs last week") and a 30-day sparkline; whole tile is a focusable Link with focus-visible ring. Sync health (failed logins, stale clients) moves to a slim status strip under the header, not a tile.
ROW 2 (above the fold on 1080p) - left col-span-8 "Action queue": a real table of notices, tabs Overdue / Due 7d / Unassigned / High priority / New since last sync, columns Client (GSTIN + trade name), Category chip, Description (truncate), Due (with "x days" badge, red if overdue, honours extended_due_date), Owner avatar/select, Amount, Priority chip, row actions (open case, mark replied, assign). Max 10 rows, "View all N" footer link to /notices-all with the same filter. Right col-span-4 "By category": Notice Summary with placeholder categories collapsed behind a "Show uncaptured categories" toggle, real rows sorted by Open desc, each row shows Open/Total as an inline bar plus counts, Replied replaced by "Awaiting reply"; clicking a category filters the queue in place (no navigation), with a visible chip and clear button.
ROW 3 - three chart cards (col-span-4 each, recharts via the existing chart.tsx): Ageing of open notices (0-7 / 8-30 / 31-90 / 90+ days, stacked by category); Issued vs closed, last 12 months (bar + line); Workload by owner (horizontal bars: open, overdue). 
ROW 4 - left col-span-8 "Clients needing attention": top 8 clients ranked by overdue then open count (replaces the "5 most recently created clients" Company card; Add/Import/Template move to the Company List page). Right col-span-4 "This week" agenda: a 7-day list of due/issue dates with counts and client names (replaces the month grid; a month view stays available via a "Calendar" toggle, using dot markers and text-foreground, never white-on-pastel). 
Responsive: tiles 6→3→2 columns at lg/md/sm; queue and category stack at <1280px; charts stack at <1024px; tables inside overflow-x-auto only. States: skeleton tiles and rows while loading, an Alert (not muted 11px text) when the extension is missing with the install link, an error Alert when any fetch fails, TableEmptyState for empty queues. Data: one react-query hook (staleTime 60s) hitting a Postgres view/RPC that returns aggregates plus the top-N queue, instead of four ad-hoc effects pulling the full table client-side.

The Notices Dashboard's numbers are not trustworthy today, and the root cause is one design decision in the extension: `replaceNotices` (extension/background.js:102-105) deletes every gst_notices row for a client and re-inserts only the portal-owned columns on every Sync All. That silently erases staff_status, priority, reply_date, assign_to, remarks, extended_due_date and any manually added notice — which is exactly why the live screenshot shows Open = Total (1060/1060), the Replied column all dashes, and "Last 24 Hours" (64) larger than "Last 15 Days" (3): pulled_at is reset for every row on every sync. On top of that, "Over Due" (473) counts closed and replied notices, ignores extended_due_date, treats a notice as overdue from 05:30 IST on its own due date (UTC parse of a date-only string), and can never include the DRC-01/ASMT-10/Enforcement case rows because the extension writes `due_date: null` for every case/task row. The KPI tiles, the Notice Summary table and the GSTIN Wise Notice Count report each use a different definition of "a notice" (per row vs per deduped case vs 1000-row-capped select), so their totals cannot reconcile, and the "Failed Logins" tile can never count an actual failed login because nothing logs one. The biggest lever is to replace delete-then-insert with an upsert keyed on (client_id, source, reference_number) that only touches portal-owned columns, then rebuild Open/Due/Overdue on a single canonical notice set that honours staff status, reply date and extended due date.

Today the litigation data model is a flat, portal-mirror schema: gst_notices (one row per portal list entry, plus 20 staff-editable columns bolted on), gst_refund_applications, gst_drc03_filings, gst_case_folder_items (raw itemJson per case folder) and client_sync_log — all with only a client_id index, no unique/natural key, no FK between them (case_id/arn are text joined by convention), no updated_at trigger, no audit trail, and RLS open to public. The single most damaging fact is the write path: every "Sync All" does DELETE-all-rows-for-client then INSERT (extension/background.js:103-104), and the re-inserted rows carry only portal columns (content.js:2532-2537), so every staff_status, priority, reply/order/submission date, amount_of_demand, remarks and assign_to — and every manually added notice from AddNoticeDialog — is silently erased on the next sync; that is why Open = Total = 1060 on the dashboard and Replied is all dashes. The biggest lever is therefore a two-step schema move: (1) stabilise gst_notices with an origin flag, a unique portal key and an upsert that touches only portal columns, so staff work survives; (2) introduce a matter layer above it. Target ERD in words: gst_matters (id, client_id, matter_no, title, matter_type [scn/asmt/audit/refund/registration/eway/other], forum [proper_officer/appellate_authority/gstat/high_court/supreme_court], stage [new→under_review→reply_drafted→reply_filed→ph_scheduled→order_received→appeal_filed→closed_*], assigned_to→profiles.user_id, counsel_id→gst_counsels, period_from/to, financial_year, authority_designation, opened_at, closed_at, closure_reason, tags text[], sla fields) 1→N gst_notices (add matter_id, origin, portal_missing_at, created_by/updated_by) 1→N gst_matter_deadlines (kind [reply_due/appeal_limitation/appeal_condonable/rectification_s161/gstat_limitation/pre_deposit/internal_target], due_on, computed_from, basis_section, is_met, met_on) ; gst_matters 1→N gst_hearings (scheduled_on, held_on, outcome [held/adjourned/ex_parte], next_date, attended_by, notes) ; gst_matters 1→N gst_demand_lines (document_ref, financial_year, act [CGST/SGST/IGST/CESS], head [tax/interest/penalty/late_fee], demanded, admitted, disputed, paid, paid_via_drc03_id→gst_drc03_filings) ; gst_drc03_filings gains matter_id + payment_purpose [voluntary/pre_deposit_s107/pre_deposit_s112/against_order] ; gst_matters 1→N gst_documents (notice_id nullable, doc_type [notice/reply/annexure/order/apl01/apl02/hearing_notes/drc03/other], storage_path in a PRIVATE bucket, sha256, uploaded_by, portal_doc_id) replacing pdf_url/documents jsonb/attachments jsonb ; gst_matters 1→N gst_matter_notes ; gst_matters 1→N gst_matter_activity (actor, action, field, old, new, at — trigger-fed) ; email_outbox gains matter_id/notice_id and new kinds so client + GST-team alerts are logged against the matter ; staff_task_reminders gains notice_id/matter_id ; gst_matter_fees (fee_type, amount, billed_on, invoice_ref) ; gst_case_folder_items gains notice_id FK and a unique key. With that in place the dashboard can compute ageing, limitation-at-risk, next hearing, owner workload and "needs attention today" from real columns instead of due_date < now.

What exists today is a returns-only email pipeline: `email_templates` (5 keys, kind CHECK 'reminder'|'confirmation'), `client_reminder_settings`, `return_reminder_schedules`, and `email_outbox` (client_id NOT NULL, single `to_email`, template_key FK, partial unique index only for confirmations), drained by `send-gst-email` (Microsoft Graph client-credentials from gst@vjdesai.com, HTML only, toRecipients only, no cc/attachments) on an hourly pg_cron plus `queue-gst-reminders` at 04:00 UTC; the only other "alerting" is in-app and ephemeral (TargetDueAlertDialog for returns due today, the private staff_task_reminders grid, a sonner toast on chat @mention) — there is not a single line of code in src/, supabase/, extension/ or agent/ that emails anyone about a notice, refund, DRC-03, due date, assignment, hearing or failed login. The biggest lever is a small event layer: fix the extension's delete-then-insert so `gst_notices` is upserted on (client_id, reference_number) with a `first_seen_at`, add a `gst_notice_events` table fed by DB triggers (new row, due-date ladder, status/assignment change, sync failure), widen `email_outbox` (new kinds, nullable client_id, cc/bcc arrays, attachments, `dedupe_key`), and add three edge functions — `notify-notice-events` (every 15 min), `queue-notice-reminders` (daily 03:30 UTC) and `notice-daily-digest` / `partner-weekly-summary` (03:00 UTC Mon–Sat / Monday) — all writing through the existing outbox so the RemindersPage log and the Graph sender are reused unchanged. Recommended event → rule → template → recipient matrix for the GST team: (1) notice.new — first time a (client, reference_number) is seen in gst_notices, batched per 15 min → `notice_new` (with notice PDF attached, portal link, due date, amount) → team list gst@vjdesai.com + assignee if any, in-app bell to all staff; (2) notice.due — staff_status not Closed and coalesce(extended_due_date, due_date) at T-7 / T-3 / T-1 / T0, then every 3 days while overdue (cap 5) → `notice_due_t7` … `notice_overdue` → assignee (fallback team list), cc gst_manager from T-1 and cc partners once overdue; (3) hearing.upcoming — new `hearing_date` at T-3 / T-1 / T0 → `notice_hearing` → assignee + partners; (4) notice.assigned — `assigned_to_user_id` changes → `notice_assigned` → the assignee's profiles.email; (5) notice.status_changed / refund.status_changed / drc03.new — row-level trigger on the three tables → folded into the daily digest, immediate email only for Refund rejected/deficiency memo and Order/DRC-07 issued; (6) sync.failed — client_sync_log status='failed' → `sync_failed` (dedupe per client per day) → team list, plus a "not synced in 7 days" line in the digest; (7) digest.daily at 08:30 IST Mon–Sat → `notice_digest_daily` (new 24h, due 7d, overdue, unassigned, failed logins, stale syncs) → team list + every superadmin/gst_manager; (8) digest.weekly Monday 09:00 IST → `partner_weekly_summary` (category counts, ageing buckets, demand-amount exposure, staff workload) → partners only; (9) client.notice_intimation — never automatic: a "Notify client" button on the notice row queues `client_notice_intimation` to clients.email with a staff-vetted preview and the PDF attached, cc team list. WhatsApp/SMS should be added later only as an extra `channel` on the same outbox row, with email remaining the system of record.

Today the "Notices Dashboard" is a document inbox, not a litigation system: gst_notices holds one row per portal document (SCN, reminder, order, LUT ack, refund ack) with a two-value Open/Closed staff_status, a free-text issued_by / financial_year / assign_to, a single amount_of_demand, and post-facto reply/order/submission fields; gst_case_folder_items keeps the raw portal case folder (INTIM/NOTCE/REPLY/ORDRS/DRC7A/APLCN/NOTAC) as JSON but nothing joins those folders into a "matter" with a stage, section, forum, authority, outcome, demand ledger, hearing or limitation date. The extension captures only get/notices, case/task/get, case/folder/items and case/search(RFUND, ADJVP) — appeals (APL-01/02/04, GSTAT), recovery (DRC-13/16/22), e-way bill (MOV), DRC-01B/01C, REG-17/21, s.128A SPL forms and summons have no capture and no typed manual-entry path. The email pipeline (email_outbox / queue-gst-reminders / send-gst-email) handles GSTR data reminders only; no notice, due-date, hearing, order or limitation alert exists. Worse, every Sync All deletes and re-inserts the client's gst_notices without the staff columns, so all litigation tracking entered so far is wiped on the next sync — this must be fixed before anything else is built. Biggest lever: introduce a first-class Matter entity with a stage machine and a rules-based deadline engine, hang the existing document rows and case-folder items off it, and drive both the dashboard (Action Centre, calendar, MIS) and the GST-team e-mails from matter stages rather than from raw document rows. Target module map — Pages: /litigation (Action Centre: due today / this week, hearings, limitation expiring ≤30d, awaiting approval, unassigned, new since last sync), /litigation/matters (list with stage, forum, exposure, owner, ageing), /litigation/matters/:id (workspace tabs: Timeline, Documents, Demand & Payments, Hearings, Deadlines, Tasks & Approvals, Correspondence, Notes), /litigation/calendar (hearing + statutory limitation + reply due), /litigation/mis (ageing, exposure by client/officer/section/FY, stage funnel, outcome/win-rate), /litigation/masters (tax_authorities, counsels, sections, reply_templates/precedents), /litigation/alerts (rule editor), client portal /portal/matters (read-only statement). Entities: litigation_matters, litigation_matter_events (links gst_notices, gst_case_folder_items, gst_refund_applications, gst_drc03_filings rows), matter_stages (reference), matter_deadlines (rule-generated, hard/soft), matter_hearings, matter_demands (per FY x head x stage: proposed/confirmed/dropped), matter_payments (pre-deposit, DRC-03 against SCN, recovery, re-credit; FK to gst_drc03_filings), matter_documents (unified repository, versioned), matter_tasks, matter_approvals, matter_notes, matter_counsels + counsels, matter_fees, tax_authorities, reply_templates, notice_alert_rules, gst_notices_audit; plus new email_outbox kinds (notice_new, notice_due, notice_overdue, hearing_reminder, order_received, limitation_warning, litigation_digest, client_matter_statement) and a queue-notice-alerts edge function on the existing pg_cron.

Portal sync today is a human-driven Chrome-extension job: "Sync All" (mode notices_bundle) opens one portal tab, and for every credentialed client a staff member types a CAPTCHA while content.js reads get/notices + case/task/get, harvests PDFs and case folders, then chains Refunds and DRC-03 before logging out and moving to the next client. Persistence is delete-all-then-insert per client (background.js replaceNotices/replaceRefundApplications/replaceDrc03Filings), so a sync is not idempotent in any useful sense: it wipes every staff workflow field (staff_status, priority, reply/order/submission data, remarks, assign_to) and every manually added notice, resets pulled_at on all rows, and on failure writes fake "PULL FAILED" rows into the data tables. That single design choice explains the screenshot's 1060/1060 Open-equals-Total, the all-dash Replied column and a "Last 24 Hours" of 64 that really means "rows re-pulled yesterday". Logging is one client_sync_log row per client from the notices step only; login failures are never detected or logged, refunds/DRC-03 failures inside the bundle are invisible, an unexpected exception stalls the job silently, and any job older than 20 minutes is dropped without trace, so "Failed Logins" is both misnamed and unreliable. The headless agent (agent/) has a queue, per-client Playwright sessions in portal_sessions and a needs_human CAPTCHA loop, but no notices job type, no app UI that enqueues jobs, a disabled schedule and a null CAPTCHA solver, so no unattended sync exists; the email pipeline (queue-gst-reminders/send-gst-email + pg_cron) knows nothing about notices. Recommended architecture: TRIGGER (Sync All or a nightly pg_cron enqueue creates a sync_runs row and one portal_jobs/queue entry per client) -> RUN (extension or agent hits the same proven JSON endpoints, then calls a single upsert_portal_notices RPC keyed on client_id+source+reference_number that preserves staff columns, sets first_seen_at/last_seen_at, and emits gst_notice_events rows for new/changed notices) -> LOG (client_sync_log gets run_id + action per step login/notices/refunds/drc03 with retry/backoff and a per-run summary; extension version recorded) -> NOTIFY (a trigger on gst_notice_events queues email_outbox rows of kind notice_alert/notice_digest to the GST team and client using the existing send-gst-email cron, plus a realtime channel that refreshes the dashboard and shows last-sync freshness per client). The biggest lever is replacing delete-then-insert with the upsert RPC and first_seen_at, because every KPI, the workflow columns and any future email alert depend on it.

Today the Notices Dashboard is a faithful clone of Notice Alert's *counting* layer (8 KPI tiles, a category table, a mini calendar, a company panel) but stops there: it has no alerting of any kind (the email pipeline in queue-gst-reminders only knows filing_status return reminders), no stage beyond Open/Closed, no owner, no hearing date, no demand-exposure figure, no charts, no staff-side document store, no activity log, and nothing a client can see. Every competitor verified (Notice Alert, ClearTax, Cygnet, GSTHero, Masters India, Turia, Jamku, GSTNoticeAI, My Notice Track) ships at least email alerts on new notice + due-date reminders and most ship owner/SLA workflow, hearing tracking and demand-at-risk views; several add WhatsApp, AI-assisted reply drafting and a client-facing status feed. The single biggest lever is wiring gst_notices into the existing email_outbox/pg_cron pipeline (new-notice digest to the GST team, 7/3/1-day due reminders, overdue escalation to the manager) — it reuses infrastructure that already exists and converts the dashboard from a scoreboard into an alerting system. Ranked features that would make this best-in-class for a mid-size CA firm: (1) email alerts + escalation to the GST team on new/due/overdue notices, with a daily digest; (2) a litigation lifecycle (Received → Reply Filed → PH → Order → Appeal → Tribunal/HC) with a case/matter grouping SCN, order and appeal; (3) named-staff assignment with a "My queue / Needs attention today" panel and staff-workload MIS; (4) demand-at-risk KPIs (tax/interest/penalty, pre-deposit, DRC-03 paid, PPR risk class) with a contingent-liability report; (5) hearing-date tracking on the calendar with hearing reminders and Google/Outlook .ics export; (6) per-notice activity log / audit trail and a staff document store (reply drafts, evidence, orders) on the case folder; (7) ageing/trend/category charts using the recharts kit already in the repo; (8) a client-portal "My Notices" view plus one-click "notify client" email with the PDF; (9) reply templates per notice form (ASMT-10, DRC-01A, REG-17, RFD-08) with an optional AI first-draft behind human review; (10) sync-freshness visibility and a scheduled agent pull so "Last 24 Hours" is not dependent on someone clicking Sync All and solving 92 CAPTCHAs.

Today the staff journey is: Sync All (extension, one CAPTCHA per client) → firm-wide gst_notices rows land with staff_status NULL → the Notices Dashboard tile drills to /notices-all, a 23-column NoticeWorkflowListView with search, 4 dropdown filters, checkbox bulk Status/Priority, an inline Open/Closed Select and a pencil "Log reply/order/submission" dialog → a Reference-No link opens AdditionalNoticeFolderPage only for case-linked rows (plain get/notices rows, the majority, have no drill-down page at all) → partner reporting is two count tables (Notice Summary, GSTIN Wise) exported to Excel only. The single biggest lever is data integrity: extension/background.js replaceNotices() deletes every gst_notices row for a client and re-inserts portal-only fields, so every re-sync silently wipes staff_status, priority, assign_to, reply/order/submission, remarks and any manually added notice — the whole workflow layer is erased on the next Sync All, which is exactly why Open equals Total (1060/1060) and Replied is all dashes. Fix that (upsert on (client_id, reference_number) preserving staff columns, and never replace real rows with a "PULL FAILED" diagnostic row), then build the missing work-item surface: a right-side Notice Drawer (or /notices/:id page) with header (client, ref, type, section, issue/due/extended due, ageing and days-to-due, demand amount, priority, assignee from profiles, enum status with reason-on-close/reopen), a tabbed body (Details | Case Folder items | Documents with inline PDF viewer | Activity timeline from a new gst_notice_events table | Emails sent), and a footer action bar (Change status, Assign, Log reply, Log order, Log hearing, Add note, Email client, Email GST team, Print status PDF). Above the list, a bulk-action toolbar on selection: Assign to, Set status (with reason), Set priority, Set extended due date, Email GST team digest, Export selected (Excel/PDF), plus saved views ("My open notices", "Due in 7 days", "Overdue & unreplied", "Unassigned", "New since last sync") and sortable columns with an Ageing and Days-to-due column colour-coded by the app's warning/destructive tokens.

gap_audits.key: gap:Live-data reconciliation of the audit's own claims (and a fixture to lock KPI definitions)
gap_audits.summary: Every number on the live Notices Dashboard reproduces exactly from the anon-key tables using the page's own formulas (Total 1060, Last 15 Days 3, Last 24 Hours 64, Total GSTIN 92, Open 1060, 7 Days Due 0, Over Due 473, Failed Logins 0; Notice Summary Refund 60/41/19 = 37 dedicated ARNs ∪ 33 distinct case ids − 10 overlap, DRC 03 183/167/16 = 53 ∪ 147 − 17) — so the tiles are arithmetically correct and semantically misleading. Graded against the data: CONFIRMED — "Last 24 Hours" is re-inserted rows of the 6 clients synced on 2026-09-12 (max issue_date in that batch 2026-07-17); "Over Due 473" is literally every row with a due_date (587 NULL, 473 < today, 0 ≥ today, max 2026-09-07) and "7 Days Due 0" is structural because extension/content.js hard-codes due_date:null for all 403 case rows while gst_case_folder_items.raw_json already holds 159 portal due-date fields and 35 hearing dates; "Failed Logins 0" disagrees today with the Company List it links to (Company List does not filter action, so 1 client shows Failed there) and can never register a real login failure; GstinWiseNoticeCountPage reads gst_notices without fetchAllRows and the 1000-row cap is live, so it silently drops 60 rows; three different totals (1060 tile, 1106 Notice Summary Total row, 1090 GSTIN-wise) coexist. REFUTED — "duplicates already present": 0 duplicate (client_id, reference_number) pairs across all 1060 rows (the 55 duplicate (client_id, case_id) pairs are legitimate multi-task rows per case, which is its own reporting problem). LATENT — "sync wipes staff data": row replacement is data-proven (103 clients synced more than once, 100% of every such client's rows carry only the latest sync's pulled_at, updated_at = created_at on 1060/1060) but no staff workflow value has ever existed to be wiped (staff_status/priority/assign_to/reply_date/order_date/submission_date/remarks/extended_due_date/amount_of_demand all 0 non-null, no manual/ PDFs, 0 PULL FAILED rows). Total GSTIN 92 vs 121 clients is simply "clients with ≥1 notice row": all 121 have credentials, 29 have no rows (16 synced with "0 entries found", 13 never synced, 8 inactive). The biggest lever is to move the KPI/category logic out of the component into pure functions locked by a vitest fixture (the task's own fixture distribution sums to 999 — it was itself a 1000-cap read; live is Notice 470, Order 187, Voluntary Payment 148, Determination Of Tax 89, LUT 65, Refunds 49, Scrutiny 19, Appeal 17, Audit 5, Waiver 4, Enforcement 4, Rectification 2, Pre-GST 1) and then redefine Open/Overdue/Due-soon from portal signals (ORDRS/CLOSR folder items, folder due dates) rather than from staff columns nobody has ever filled.

gap_audits.key: gap:Trust boundary between the web app, the Chrome extension and Supabase storage (postMessage origin, host match, anyone-can-delete PDF policy, credential display)
gap_audits.summary: The notices/litigation surface has no enforced trust boundary anywhere: the Chrome extension's app bridge (extension/appbridge.js:15) accepts window messages from any origin and any frame, is injected into every "https://*.vercel.app/*" page (extension/manifest.json:32) but NOT into the real production origin gst.vjdesai.com (which is why the live screenshot says "Extension not detected" and Sync All is dead in production), and every one of its 12 __gstk* messages ends in background.js reading clients.gst_user_id/gst_password with the anon key and logging into the GST portal. Scanned show-cause notices, orders, refund and DRC-03 PDFs (734 notice PDFs + 879 case-folder attachments, live-confirmed) sit in the public return-pdfs bucket under guessable paths notices/<clientId>/<referenceNumber>.pdf; a plain unauthenticated GET returns 206 application/pdf, and the bucket carries "Anyone can upload/view/delete/update return PDFs" policies for the public role, so the anon key shipped in extension/config.js:5 and the app bundle can read, overwrite or wipe every litigation document. On top of the accepted "RLS open to public" design (121 clients, all 121 with a plaintext gst_password, 1060 notices, 37 refunds, 53 DRC-03, 408 sync-log rows, 123 portal_jobs readable and writable by any authenticated client user via devtools), two app-level bugs make the situation worse without devtools at all: AuthContext restores the role from the localStorage blob without re-reading user_roles (a client can rewrite role:'superadmin'), and /clients has no staff gate so any client login can open the Credentials tab where passwords are shown unmasked by default. The biggest lever before any e-mail alert carries a PDF link is to make return-pdfs private and mint short-lived signed URLs from an edge function (or proxy through one), drop the anyone-can-delete/update policies, then fix the bridge (origin + source check, exact production host), the session-role bug and the credentials gate. Until those five are done, every notice e-mail would be a permanent public link to a demand order that anyone who forwards it can open, and every forwarded link reveals the client's internal id and the notice reference number.

gap_audits.key: gap:Deletion, retention, backup and recovery of litigation records (cascade deletes, no soft delete, no version history, no audit trail on client deletion)
gap_audits.summary: Litigation records in this app have no retention layer at all: gst_notices, gst_case_folder_items, gst_refund_applications, gst_drc03_filings and client_sync_log all hang off clients with ON DELETE CASCADE, there is no soft-delete column, no BEFORE/AFTER DELETE trigger, no history/snapshot table, no storage-object cleanup and no backup/PITR documentation anywhere in the repo (grep over docs/, README.md, CLAUDE.md, agent/, extension/ and supabase/config.toml returns nothing). The two live data-loss paths are (1) a one-click client delete from CompanyListPage/ClientsPage, gated only by delete_clients, that wipes the entire notice/order/refund/DRC-03 history plus the version and sync logs, orphans every PDF in the public bucket and writes nothing to audit_log, and (2) the extension's delete-all-then-insert sync, which is non-transactional, is triggerable by any staff member, wipes manually added notices and every staff-entered workflow field (status, priority, assignee, reply/order details) on every run, and on any portal error replaces the whole history with a single "PULL FAILED" row. Because the anon key is embedded in the SPA bundle and the extension and every policy is FOR ALL TO public, any of these tables or bucket objects can also be deleted by anyone holding the key without logging in. Against s.36 CGST (retain records 72 months from the annual-return due date, and while any appeal/proceeding is pending, one year after its final disposal) every path rated here is irreversible and unlogged. The biggest lever is a single migration that adds an archive table fed by BEFORE DELETE/UPDATE triggers on the four litigation tables, flips the client FK to RESTRICT behind a soft-delete flag, and moves the extension's replace into a server-side upsert RPC; that alone closes both loss paths and gives the firm a restore button modelled on the existing twob_versions flow.

gap_audits.key: gap:Role-by-role walkthrough of who can do what on the notices surface (employee, gst_manager, superadmin, client) — the permission matrix was never mapped
gap_audits.summary: The notices/litigation surface today has a two-level access model: any of the three staff roles (superadmin, gst_manager, employee) can open every notices page, every client's notice list, PDFs, case folders, exports, sync logs and even plain-text GST portal passwords, while the client role is redirected off every notices route and has no notice view at all. The only grantable notice key is edit_notice_status (UserControlPage.tsx:122), which bundles add-notice, inline Open/Closed, priority, bulk status/priority, the reply/order/submission dialog, free-text assign-to and the per-row "open on portal" icon into one switch; gst_manager is indistinguishable from superadmin because hasPermission() returns true for both (AuthContext.tsx:479-481). Several gates are inconsistent or cosmetic: Sync All and Company List Sync/Fetch are open to every staff member (contrary to the brief), the export_data key exists but is never called anywhere, /add-client and /edit-client/:id have no guard so the hidden pencil icon protects nothing, and because every notice table's RLS is FOR ALL TO public (by design, auth.uid() is NULL), every UI gate can be bypassed with the anon key that ships in the bundle. There is no per-employee data scoping anywhere in src or migrations to build a "my matters" queue on: gst_notices.assign_to is a free-text column, and no assigned_clients/staff_clients table exists. The biggest lever is a small set of new keys (sync_notices, assign_notice, close_notice, delete_notice, view_portal_credentials, export_notices, notify_client) plus an assigned_to uuid FK and a client-scoped read-only notice view, which together turn the current staff/non-staff binary into the partner / manager / senior / article / client model a CA litigation practice needs. Separately, the extension manifest only injects the app bridge on *.vercel.app, so on the live gst.vjdesai.com domain Sync All, Portal-open and Login are dead for every role, which is what the screenshot's "Extension not detected" hint is showing.

gap_audits.key: gap:Institutional knowledge: the notices module has no positions document, no staff SOP and no runbook — while the audit proposes rewriting rules that are currently encoded only in code comments
gap_audits.summary: The notices/refunds/DRC-03 module carries at least 30 elected positions and firm decisions (category taxonomy, Refunds/Voluntary-Payment ARN dedupe, Open = staff_status only, Last-24-Hours = pulled_at, Over Due ignores Closed, Sync All open to every employee, 20-minute job expiry, 3x session-drop retry then a PULL FAILED sentinel, no auto-CAPTCHA) but every one of them exists only as a dated code comment — there is no docs/NOTICES_*.md, CLAUDE.md has no notices section, extension/README.md still describes the v1 filing-status/ledger extension, and the git history was squashed on 2026-08-27 so the 2026-08-24/25/26 decisions referenced in comments cannot be recovered from commit messages. Several of those comments are already stale or contradictory (UNCAPTURED_NOTICE_CATEGORIES vs CASE_NOTICE_TYPE_MAP; "same definition" for Failed Logins vs an unfiltered Company List query; the migration header claiming no automation exists) and two live operational gaps have nobody to read about them: the production domain gst.vjdesai.com is not in the extension manifest (hence "Extension not detected" in the screenshot) and a failed pull silently deletes a client's prior notices and leaves a sentinel row that the dashboard counts as an open notice. The biggest lever is to write docs/NOTICES_LITIGATION_FLOW.md now — a positions register tagged KEEP / CONFIRM-WITH-FIRM / REPLACE, the data flow, the tile and Open/Closed definitions, the sync SOP and failure runbook — plus a CLAUDE.md paragraph in the Builder/2B style, before any of the other audit dimensions rewrite the tiles, taxonomy or workflow and silently discard the current elections.

gap_audits.key: gap:Refunds and DRC-03 surfaces were listed in scope but received no dedicated findings (merge of dedicated tables with case rows, regex-derived closure, amounts never surfaced, document jsonb shapes)
gap_audits.summary: The Refund and DRC-03 half of the notices family is stitched together from two capture paths that disagree: the dedicated tables (gst_refund_applications: 37 rows across 3 clients; gst_drc03_filings: 53 rows across 8 clients) and the 'Refunds' / 'Voluntary Payment' case-stub rows in gst_notices (49 rows / 4 clients and 148 rows / 38 clients). Re-deriving by hand from live anon-key reads reproduces the panel exactly (Refund 60/41/19, DRC 03 183/167/16), so the arithmetic is faithful, but the semantics are wrong: 131 of the 167 "open" DRC-03s are portal acknowledgements of accepted payments and 22 of the 41 "open" refunds end in an RFD-06/PMT-03 order, all counted open only because case stubs have no staff_status; the same 197 stub rows inflate the dashboard's Total/Open Notices tiles to 1060/1060. The richest data the firm actually holds (DRC-03 payment breakdowns for 126 more cases worth Rs 6.46 Cr, RFD-05/06 sanctioned amounts worth Rs 7.72 Cr, 22 RFD-08 reply due dates, cause-of-payment codes and SCN references) is already in gst_case_folder_items.raw_json and is never lifted into the tables the pages read, so drill-downs show zeros, "Sanctioned Amount" is hard-coded null, and no refund deadline ever reaches the 7-Days-Due / Over-Due tiles. Two extension write patterns (delete-then-insert without the documents column; a 'PULL FAILED' sentinel that replaces a client's history) actively lose data on every re-sync or transient portal error. The biggest lever is one canonical refund/DRC-03 case model: promote the captured folder JSON (amounts, due dates, cause code, SCN link) into typed columns with a staff workflow layer, derive open/closed from the latest event instead of a wording regex, and only then put rupee KPIs and a deadline queue on the dashboard and feed an email digest to the GST team.

confirmed_broken.title: Sync All deletes and re-inserts gst_notices, wiping staff status/priority/assignee - root cause of Open = Total (1060/1060)
confirmed_broken.evidence: replaceNotices: async (clientId, rows) => { await del('gst_notices', `client_id=eq.${clientId}`); return rows.length ? post('gst_notices', rows) : true; } - content.js builds rows from the portal only (grep for staff_status/assign_to/priority in extension/content.js returns nothing) and no migration adds a trigger that re-applies them; staff_status, priority, reply_date, assign_to etc. were added by supabase/migrations/20260824100700_gst_notices_workflow_tracking.sql and 20260824104900_gst_notices_extra_fields.sql.
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Every time anyone presses Sync All, all Open/Closed marks, priority tiers, reply/order/submission logs and owners entered by the GST team for that client are destroyed. The dashboard then truthfully reports that nothing is closed and nothing is replied, which makes every KPI and the Notice Summary meaningless for managing litigation.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Add a unique key on gst_notices (client_id, source, coalesce(reference_number, case_id, description hash)) and switch replaceNotices to a PostgREST upsert (Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates) that only writes portal-sourced columns; or, before the delete, SELECT the staff columns keyed by reference_number and re-apply them after insert. Add a DB-level regression check (count of non-null staff_status before/after a sync).

reasons: CONFIRM: Confirmed by code trace. extension/background.js:102-105 `replaceNotices: async (clientId, rows) => { await del('gst_notices', `client_id=eq.${clientId}`); return rows.length ? post('gst_notices', rows) : true; }` is an unconditional delete-all-then-insert per client (not even scoped by source). The notice rows content.js builds at lines 2532-2535 and 2609-2611 contain only portal fields (`client_id, source: 'notices', reference_number, notice_type, ...`); grep for staff_status/assign_to/reply_date/priority in extension/content.js and background.js returns nothing except the unrelated `priority: 1` in a job queue. No migration touching gst_notices declares a trigger (grep -i trigger over the seven gst_notices migrations returns nothing) and no src/lib code re-applies staff columns after a sync. background.js does know how to do true upserts (lines 65, 132-148, 173-176 for filing_status / taxpayer_profile / filed returns) but deliberately chose delete-then-insert here. So every Sync All wipes staff_status/priority/reply_*/order_*/submission_*/assign_to/remarks/extended_due_date for that client. The 'root cause of 1060/1060' framing is plausible rather than proven (staff may also simply never have marked rows), but the data-loss mechanism is real and unguarded, and the Refund row (60/41/19) showing closed counts only because it is derived from portal status rather than staff_status is consistent with it.

CONFIRM: Confirmed. extension/background.js:102-105 `replaceNotices` does `del('gst_notices', 'client_id=eq.'+clientId)` then `post('gst_notices', rows)`. The rows built in extension/content.js:2532-2538 (get/notices) and 2609-2614 (case/task) contain only portal columns (client_id, source, reference_number, notice_type, description, issue_date, due_date, status, issued_by, case_id, pdf_url) — no staff_status/priority/reply_*/order_*/submission_*/assign_to/remarks/extended_due_date. No migration touching gst_notices declares any trigger (grep for trigger across migrations referencing gst_notices returns nothing). Staff edits in src/components/reports/views/NoticeWorkflowListView.tsx:404/435/455/496 update by `id`, and the id is regenerated on every re-insert, so even in-flight UI references break. Worse than stated: the delete has no `source` filter, so manually entered notices from src/components/notices/AddNoticeDialog.tsx:73-87 (source 'notices', staff_status 'Open', uploaded PDF) are also wiped by the next Sync All of that client. Caveat on causality: Open = Total could also simply reflect staff never having marked anything Closed (AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:166 notes 'most rows have staff_status = null'), so 'root cause' is plausible rather than proven — but the wipe makes any marking futile regardless. Fix soundness: the proposed expression key `coalesce(reference_number, case_id, description hash)` cannot be used with PostgREST's `?on_conflict=` parameter (it maps to ON CONFLICT (column list), not expression indexes). Better: add a stored generated column `dedupe_key text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (coalesce(reference_number, case_id, md5(description))) STORED`, a unique index on (client_id, source, dedupe_key), and call `post('gst_notices?on_conflict=client_id,source,dedupe_key', rows, 'return=minimal,resolution=merge-duplicates')` — the existing `post` helper (background.js:50) already accepts a `prefer` argument. Because the payload carries only portal columns, merge-duplicates leaves staff columns intact and ids stable. The alternative SELECT-then-reapply approach also works but is two extra round trips per client and races with concurrent staff edits.

confirmed_broken.title: "Last 24 Hours" counts rows rewritten by the last sync, not newly issued notices
confirmed_broken.evidence: const last24Hours = displayRows.filter((r) => daysAgo(r.pulled_at) <= 1).length; - pulled_at defaults to now() on insert (20260817180000_notices_refund_drc03.sql line 22) and every sync re-inserts all rows (background.js:103-104), so the tile equals 'all notices of whichever clients were synced today' (64 on the screenshot).
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: A manager reads 64 as 'sixty-four new notices arrived today' and either panics or learns to ignore the tile. Either way the one tile that should surface fresh portal activity is noise.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Add first_seen_at timestamptz to gst_notices preserved across upserts (see finding 1); rename the tile 'New since last sync' and count first_seen_at > previous successful sync time from client_sync_log. Show the sync time in the tile caption.

reasons: CONFIRM: Confirmed. src/pages/NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:254 `const last24Hours = displayRows.filter((r) => daysAgo(r.pulled_at) <= 1).length;`. supabase/migrations/20260817180000_notices_refund_drc03.sql:22 `pulled_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`; content.js never sets pulled_at on notice rows (grep shows pulled_at only for other tables at 2213/2273/3821), and replaceNotices re-inserts every row on each sync, so every synced client's full history gets a fresh pulled_at. The drill-down page is honest about this — AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:80 labels the filter 'pulled from the portal in the last 24 hours' and line 171 uses the same predicate — so tile and list agree; only the tile caption 'Last 24 Hours' (next to 'Last 15 Days' which IS issue_date-based, line 253) misleads. Because the drill-down explains the real meaning and nothing is lost, this is a mislabelled metric rather than a high-severity defect; downgrading to medium.

CONFIRM: Confirmed mechanically: NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:254 `daysAgo(r.pulled_at) <= 1`; gst_notices.pulled_at is `timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` (20260817180000_notices_refund_drc03.sql:22) and the extension rows never set pulled_at, so every re-inserted row gets the sync time. After a Sync All that reaches N clients, the tile equals the full historical notice count of those N clients. The drill-down page even labels the filter honestly as 'pulled from the portal in the last 24 hours' (AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:80), while the tile sits beside 'Last 15 Days' which is issue_date-based (line 253) — an inconsistent pair of semantics under similar labels. Severity is medium rather than high: it is a misleading label/metric, not a data-corrupting bug, and the drill-down explains it. Fix depends on finding 0 (first_seen_at is only preservable once sync stops deleting rows); with an upsert, `first_seen_at timestamptz DEFAULT now()` omitted from the payload is preserved automatically and 'New since last sync' can be computed against client_sync_log (20260828100000_client_sync_log.sql). Keep the existing pulled_at filter for the drill-down so /notices-all?filter=last24h still works.

confirmed_broken.title: Over Due (473) includes closed and replied notices, ignores extended_due_date, and counts today-due items as overdue from 05:30 IST
confirmed_broken.evidence: const overdue = displayRows.filter((r) => r.due_date && daysUntil(r.due_date) < 0).length; with daysUntil = (v) => (new Date(v).getTime() - now) / DAY_MS (line 249). new Date('2026-09-13') is UTC midnight = 05:30 IST, so a notice due today is 'overdue' for most of the working day; no isClosed / reply_date / extended_due_date check, although extended_due_date exists (20260824104900_gst_notices_extra_fields.sql line 11) and AllClientsNoticesPage selects it (line 127).
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: 473 of 1060 'overdue' next to '7 Days Due 0' is the contradiction the principal noticed. The number is inflated by historical, already-handled notices and by same-day due items, so the firm cannot use it to drive urgency or to email the GST team about genuine lapses.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Compute due = extended_due_date ?? due_date on a local-midnight date (parse Y-M-D parts), exclude isClosed(staff_status) and rows with reply_date/submission_date, and define '7 Days Due' as 0 <= days <= 7 inclusive of today. Share one dueDays() helper with AllClientsNoticesPage so the tile and its drill-down agree.

reasons: CONFIRM: Confirmed on all three sub-claims. NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:250 `daysUntil = (v) => (v ? (new Date(v).getTime() - now) / DAY_MS : -Infinity)` and :258 `overdue = displayRows.filter((r) => r.due_date && daysUntil(r.due_date) < 0)` — no isClosed/reply_date check (openNotices at :256 does use isClosed, so the tile set is internally inconsistent). extended_due_date is not even in the dashboard's select (:148) though the column exists (20260824104900 line 11) and AllClientsNoticesPage selects it (:126). `new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')` parses as UTC midnight, so from 05:30 IST on the due day daysUntil goes negative and the item moves from 'due7' (:257 requires >= 0) into 'overdue'. The sibling drill-down AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:158,172-173 duplicates the identical predicates, so the tile and its list agree but are both wrong in the same way; nothing elsewhere corrects it. Minor overreach: a reply_date alone does not necessarily mean the matter is no longer overdue (a reply may be filed late), so 'replied' exclusion is a design choice, but closed-inclusion and the timezone/extended-date issues are real defects in the headline number.

CONFIRM: Confirmed on all three points. (1) due_date is a Postgres `date` column, PostgREST returns 'YYYY-MM-DD', and `new Date('2026-09-13')` is UTC midnight = 05:30 IST, so from 05:30 onward a notice due today has daysUntil < 0 and is counted in Over Due (line 258) and excluded from 7 Days Due (line 257 requires >= 0). (2) No isClosed/reply_date guard on either tile — lines 257-258 filter only on due_date; isClosed is imported and used only for Open Notices (line 256). (3) extended_due_date exists (20260824104900_gst_notices_extra_fields.sql:11) and is selected by AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:126 but the dashboard select (line 148) does not fetch it and nothing reads it for due logic. The 'contradiction' framing is slightly overstated — 473 overdue with 0 due-in-7-days is not logically contradictory, just uninformative. The fix is sound; note that AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:157-158,172-173 uses byte-identical daysUntil logic, so tile and drill-down currently agree (both wrong the same way) — the shared helper must be adopted in both files in the same change or the tile will diverge from its drill-down. Excluding rows with reply_date from Over Due is a defensible firm position but should be surfaced as a choice (a replied notice may still await an order).

confirmed_broken.title: Calendar 'Both' days render white digits on a pale amber tint - unreadable
confirmed_broken.evidence: const bg = marker?.issue && marker?.due ? 'bg-warning/20 text-warning-foreground' : ... - in src/index.css --warning-foreground is '0 0% 100%' (white), so the day number is white on hsl(38 92% 50%) at 20% alpha over a white card.
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Days that have both an issue and a due date are exactly the busiest days, and they are the ones whose number disappears. The day-2/day-7 tint on the screenshot is visible only because those days are single-marker.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Use text-foreground on all tinted days and mark categories with 4px dots below the number (info/destructive/warning) instead of background tints; or drop the month grid in favour of a 'This week' agenda list.

reasons: CONFIRM: Confirmed for the light theme. NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:498 `const bg = marker?.issue && marker?.due ? 'bg-warning/20 text-warning-foreground' : ...`; src/index.css:47-48 `--warning: 38 92% 50%; --warning-foreground: 0 0% 100%;` and tailwind.config.ts:58-61 maps `warning.foreground` to that token, so 'Both' days render white digits on a 20%-alpha amber over a white card. The other two branches (:499-500) use text-destructive / text-info which are readable. Severity medium is reasonable for an unreadable date on the busiest days, though the affected surface is a small widget.

CONFIRM: Confirmed. NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:498 applies `bg-warning/20 text-warning-foreground` for days with both markers; src/index.css:48 defines `--warning-foreground: 0 0% 100%` (white) and there is no dark-mode override (only one definition in the file), tailwind.config.ts:59-60 maps it to `warning.foreground`. The cell sits inside a white Card, so the digit is white on ~20%-alpha amber over white — effectively invisible in light mode. Realistic data: 'Both' days occur whenever any notice's issue_date equals another's due_date in the shown month, common at month ends and for 30-day SCN windows. Fix is sound; dots under the digit avoid the contrast problem entirely and match the legend at lines 519-523.

confirmed_broken.title: PULL FAILED diagnostic rows are stored in gst_notices and counted as notices in every tile and in the Notice Summary
confirmed_broken.evidence: await GSTKdb.replaceNotices(cur.clientId, [{ client_id: cur.clientId, source: 'notices', description: 'PULL FAILED: ' + ... }]) (also lines 195 and 2744). The dashboard loads (q) => q.eq('source', 'notices') with no description filter (NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:143) and classifyNoticeCategory returns r.notice_type || 'Uncategorised' (noticeCategoryClassifier.ts:47); grep 'PULL FAILED' in src/ returns nothing.
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Each failed login adds a fake notice with no type, inflating Total Notices / Total GSTIN / Open and producing a stray 'Uncategorised' row in the summary; it also erases the client's real notices (the sentinel replaces them).
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Stop writing sentinels into gst_notices - client_sync_log already records status/message per client (20260828100000_client_sync_log.sql). Until then, filter description NOT ILIKE 'PULL FAILED%' in every gst_notices reader and never replace a client's rows on failure.

reasons: CONFIRM: Confirmed. extension/content.js:2471 (get/notices fetch failure), :195 (session-drop) and :2744 (DB write error) each call `GSTKdb.replaceNotices(cur.clientId, [{ client_id, source: 'notices', description: 'PULL FAILED: ...' }])`, which per background.js:102-105 first deletes every gst_notices row for that client and then inserts the sentinel — so a failed pull erases the client's real history and leaves one fake row. The dashboard's only filter is `(q) => q.eq('source', 'notices')` (NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:149); the sentinel carries source 'notices' and null notice_type, so classifyNoticeCategory (noticeCategoryClassifier.ts:47 `const type = r.notice_type || 'Uncategorised'`) buckets it as 'Uncategorised', it counts in Total/Open (staff_status null => open), and grep 'PULL FAILED' across src/ and agent/src returns nothing — no reader filters it. Sibling pages (AllClientsNoticesPage, CompanyProfilePage:136, NoticeSummaryReportPage) use the same source-only filter. client_sync_log (20260828100000) already records the failure separately, so the sentinel is redundant as well as harmful. High is appropriate.

CONFIRM: Confirmed. Three failure paths write a sentinel row into gst_notices via replaceNotices: extension/content.js:195 (session bounced 3x), 2471 (get/notices HTTP/parse failure), 2744 (DB write error). Each row is `{ client_id, source: 'notices', description: 'PULL FAILED: ...' }` with notice_type null, so classifyNoticeCategory (noticeCategoryClassifier.ts:47) yields 'Uncategorised' and it appears as an extra real row in the summary (extraRealRows, noticeSummaryReport.ts:139). The dashboard's only filter is `.eq('source','notices')` (line 149); `grep -rn 'PULL FAILED' src/` returns nothing, so no reader excludes it. Because replaceNotices deletes first, the failure also erases the client's previously pulled rows (and manual AddNoticeDialog rows) until the next successful sync — at line 2744 the delete has already succeeded before the insert failed, so the real rows are gone either way. Realistic scale is bounded (one sentinel per failed client; the screenshot shows Failed Logins 0 so possibly none right now), but it is genuine data loss plus KPI pollution. Fix is sound: client_sync_log already receives logSyncAttempt on every one of these paths (lines 196, 2472, 2745), so the sentinel is redundant; drop the replaceNotices calls in those catch blocks and, as a belt-and-braces measure, add `.not('description','ilike','PULL FAILED%')` in the dashboard/summary/GSTIN-count readers.

confirmed_broken.title: NoticesTopNav shows 'Dashboard' as active on every page in the family
confirmed_broken.evidence: { label: 'Dashboard', icon: LayoutDashboard, to: '/notices-dashboard', active: true }, ... active: false - a static array, no useLocation; the same component is rendered by NoticeSummaryReportPage.tsx:94, GstinWiseNoticeCountPage and CompanyListPage.
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: On Report > Notice Summary or Company List the pill group still highlights 'Dashboard', and the 'Notice' and 'Submission' pills are never shown active, so users lose their place inside the module.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Derive active from useLocation().pathname + search (matchPath for /notices-all with filter=submitted), or replace the pill group with the shadcn Tabs component in underline style and NavLink children.

reasons: CONFIRM: Confirmed. src/components/notices/NoticesTopNav.tsx:17-21 is a static NAV_LINKS array with `active: true` hard-coded on Dashboard and `active: false` on Notice/Submission; the component imports only Link (line 12), never useLocation, and navItemClass(item.active) (:23-26,32) renders the highlight from that constant. The Report dropdown trigger is always navItemClass(false) (:38). The component is rendered on seven pages: NoticesDashboardPage:329, CompanyListPage:252, CompanyProfilePage:269, NoticeSummaryReportPage:94, GstinWiseNoticeCountPage:148, AdditionalNoticeFolderPage:446 — so 'Dashboard' is highlighted on every one of them. Medium is fair.

CONFIRM: Confirmed. src/components/notices/NoticesTopNav.tsx:17-21 is a static NAV_LINKS array with `active: true` hard-coded on Dashboard and `active: false` on Notice/Submission; the component imports only Link (line 12), never useLocation. It is rendered by seven pages (NoticesDashboardPage, CompanyListPage, CompanyProfilePage, NoticeSummaryReportPage, GstinWiseNoticeCountPage, AdditionalNoticeFolderPage, plus the component file itself), so 'Dashboard' is highlighted on every one of them. confirmed_broken.title: Sidebar loses its active item on all Notices sub-routes
confirmed_broken.evidence: { label: 'Notices Dashboard', path: '/notices-dashboard', ... } rendered through <NavLink to={item.path}> (line 370); routes /notices-all, /notices-company-list, /notices-company/:id, /notices-report, /notices-gstin-wise-count, /refunds-all, /drc03-all (App.tsx:106-114) do not start with /notices-dashboard, so isActive is false. NAV_GROUPS already has a prefix-match pattern at line 257 that this item does not use.
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Seven of the eight pages in the module show no highlighted sidebar entry; combined with the top-nav bug the user has no orientation cue at all.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Add an optional activePrefixes: ['/notices-', '/refunds-all', '/drc03-all'] to NavItem and compute isActive with location.pathname.startsWith in navLinkClasses.

confirmed_broken.title: Every Sync All wipes staff workflow data and manually added notices (delete-then-insert)
confirmed_broken.evidence: replaceNotices: async (clientId, rows) => { await del('gst_notices', `client_id=eq.${clientId}`); return rows.length ? post('gst_notices', rows) : true; }  — and the re-inserted row (extension/content.js:2532-2536) carries only client_id, source, reference_number, notice_type, description, issue_date, due_date, status, issued_by, case_id, pdf_url. staff_status, priority, reply_ref_number, reply_date, order_number, order_date, submission_arn, submission_date, extended_due_date, amount_of_demand, remarks, financial_year, assign_to (all written by NoticeWorkflowListView.saveEdit at src/components/reports/views/NoticeWorkflowListView.tsx:496-509) are never re-written. AddNoticeDialog rows (src/components/notices/AddNoticeDialog.tsx:73-86, source='notices', no reference back to the portal) are deleted by the same `del`. No unique index exists on gst_notices (supabase/migrations/20260817180000_notices_refund_drc03.sql:12-26 defines only the uuid PK).
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Reproduction: mark a notice Closed, set a reply date and assign it to a staff member, then run Sync All — after the sync the same notice is Open again with no reply date and no assignee, and any notice added via 'Add Notice' is gone. This is why the live dashboard shows Open Notices 1060 = Total Notices 1060 and a Replied column of dashes: the firm's litigation tracking is being destroyed on every pull. For a CA firm this is the single most dangerous behaviour in the module — a closed matter re-opens, an assigned matter loses its owner, and a manually logged notice (e.g. one served by post) vanishes.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Add a unique index on gst_notices (client_id, source, reference_number) (with a partial index or coalesce for null reference_number, e.g. coalesce(reference_number, case_id, id::text)). Change replaceNotices to a PostgREST upsert (`Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates`, `on_conflict=client_id,source,reference_number`) that sends ONLY portal-owned columns so existing staff columns are preserved by the merge; never delete rows wholesale — instead mark rows the portal no longer returns with a `portal_missing_at` timestamp. Exclude rows with `entered_by`/manual flag (add a boolean `manual_entry` column set by AddNoticeDialog) from any reconciliation. Apply the same pattern to replaceRefundApplications / replaceDrc03Filings (background.js:109-112, 126-129).

reasons: CONFIRM: Traced end to end. extension/background.js:102-105 `replaceNotices` runs `del('gst_notices', client_id=eq.X)` with no source/manual filter, then POSTs the freshly scraped rows. Both row shapes the extension builds (content.js:2532-2536 get/notices rows, 2609-2614 case-task rows) carry only client_id/source/reference_number/notice_type/description/issue_date/due_date/status/issued_by/case_id/pdf_url — none of the staff columns added by 20260824100700 (staff_status, reply_*, order_*, submission_*) or 20260824104900 (extended_due_date, amount_of_demand, remarks, financial_year, assign_to) or priority (20260825120000). grep of extension/*.js for staff_status/assign_to/reply_date returns nothing, so there is no read-before-delete preservation. AddNoticeDialog.tsx:73-86 inserts with source='notices' and staff_status='Open' and is therefore deleted by the same client_id-only DELETE. No trigger or unique index on gst_notices exists in any migration (only idx_gst_notices_client at 20260817180000:27). background.js:99-101 comment even documents 'delete-all-then-insert per client'. Same pattern at 109-112 and 126-129.

CONFIRM: Confirmed. extension/background.js:102-105 `replaceNotices: async (clientId, rows) => { await del('gst_notices', \`client_id=eq.${clientId}\`); return rows.length ? post('gst_notices', rows) : true; }` is an unconditional per-client DELETE then INSERT. The rows re-inserted (content.js:2532-2536 get/notices loop and :2609-2614 task loop) carry only client_id, source, reference_number, notice_type, description, issue_date, due_date, status, issued_by, case_id, pdf_url. `grep staff_status|reply_date|assign_to|extended_due_date extension/` returns nothing — the extension never reads existing staff columns back before deleting, and there is no trigger on gst_notices in any migration (grep TRIGGER over the 7 gst_notices migrations returns nothing). AddNoticeDialog.tsx:73-86 inserts with `source: 'notices'` and no manual-entry flag, so the same `client_id=eq.X` DELETE removes it. Only index is `idx_gst_notices_client (client_id)` (20260817180000:27). With real rows (staff_status='Closed', reply_date set, assign_to set), one Sync All reverts all of them to null — this matches the live Open=Total=1060 and all-dash Replied column. Fix caveats: (1) PostgREST `on_conflict=` must name real columns backed by a non-partial unique index, so a coalesce expression/partial index will not work — add a generated column (e.g. `sync_key text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (coalesce(reference_number, case_id)) STORED`) and a unique index on (client_id, source, sync_key); task rows with null refId AND null arn, and the PULL FAILED marker rows, would have a null key so drop those writes first (finding 1). (2) Existing gst_notices already contains duplicate case rows (content.js:2607 dedupes only by refId), so a one-off de-dup is needed before the unique index can be created. (3) merge-duplicates only updates columns present in the payload, so staff columns are preserved as long as the extension keeps sending portal-owned columns only.

confirmed_broken.title: GSTIN Wise Notice Count is capped at 1000 rows and double-counts refund/DRC-03 cases, so it disagrees with Notice Summary

Then lines 97-113 count every gst_notices row (including the 'Refunds' and 'Voluntary Payment' case rows) AND add every gst_refund_applications / gst_drc03_filings row with no ARN dedupe — the exact double count computeNoticeSummary avoids (noticeSummaryReport.ts:66-76, 85, 100-122). The file header (lines 4-7) claims its grand total 'matches Notice Summary's grand total exactly'.
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Reproduction: open Report > GSTIN Wise Notice Count and compare its Total row with Report > Notice Summary's Total — they differ (about 60 rows dropped by the cap, ~20 refund/DRC-03 cases counted twice). A partner using this page to see which client carries the most open matters gets wrong per-client numbers, and the last ~60 rows of the table (arbitrary, since there is no ORDER BY) are missing entirely.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Use fetchAllRows for gst_notices (select case_id and notice_type too) and reuse the per-category dedupe: skip notice_type in ('Refunds','Voluntary Payment') in the notices loop, and merge dedicated refund/DRC-03 rows with those case rows by ARN/case_id per client exactly as mergeIntoCategory does — ideally by extracting that merge into a shared helper in noticeSummaryReport.ts that both pages call.

reasons: CONFIRM: GstinWiseNoticeCountPage.tsx:63 is a plain `supabase.from('gst_notices').select('client_id, description, staff_status, reply_date').eq('source','notices')` with no .range() loop; fetchAllRows.ts:1-8 documents the 1000-row PostgREST cap and 1055+ rows on file. Lines 97-113 count every gst_notices row (the select does not even fetch notice_type so 'Refunds'/'Voluntary Payment' case rows cannot be skipped) and then add every gst_refund_applications/gst_drc03_filings row with no ARN dedupe — whereas computeNoticeSummary (noticeSummaryReport.ts:85, 100-122) skips those types and unions by ARN. Header lines 4-7 claim the grand total matches Notice Summary exactly; it cannot.

CONFIRM: Confirmed. GstinWiseNoticeCountPage.tsx:63 `supabase.from('gst_notices').select('client_id, description, staff_status, reply_date').eq('source', 'notices')` — a plain, unordered select, while fetchAllRows.ts:1-8 documents the 1000-row PostgREST cap and 1055+ rows. Lines 97-113 then count every gst_notices row (including notice_type 'Refunds'/'Voluntary Payment' case rows — the select does not even fetch notice_type/case_id to exclude them) and add every gst_refund_applications/gst_drc03_filings row with no ARN dedupe; computeNoticeSummary (noticeSummaryReport.ts:85, 100-122) explicitly skips those two types and unions by ARN. The header comment (:4-7) claims the grand total matches Notice Summary; it cannot. Fix is sound (fetchAllRows + reuse of mergeIntoCategory per client). Severity: a wrong report, not data loss — medium.

confirmed_broken.title: A notice is 'Over Due' from 05:30 IST on its own due date (UTC parse of date-only strings)
confirmed_broken.evidence: const daysUntil = (v: string | null) => (v ? (new Date(v).getTime() - now) / DAY_MS : -Infinity);  — due_date is a Postgres `date` returned as 'YYYY-MM-DD'; `new Date('2026-09-13')` is 2026-09-13T00:00:00Z = 05:30 IST, so from 05:30 IST on the due day daysUntil < 0 → counted at line 258 as overdue and excluded from dueSoon (line 257). Identical helpers in AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:157-158 and CompanyProfilePage.tsx:218-219.
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Reproduction: a notice due today (13/09/2026) shows in 'Over Due' for the whole working day while the reply can still be filed until midnight; it never appears in '7 Days Due' on its final day. Staff see a matter flagged late when it is still within time.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Compare date-only strings: const todayIso = local YYYY-MM-DD; overdue = due < todayIso; dueSoon = due >= todayIso && due <= todayIso+7d (compute the +7 by constructing new Date(y, m-1, d+7) locally). Put it in the shared noticeDueState helper.

reasons: CONFIRM: NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:250 `new Date(v).getTime() - now` where v is a Postgres `date` column ('YYYY-MM-DD'); ECMAScript parses date-only ISO strings as UTC midnight, i.e. 05:30 IST. After that moment on the due day daysUntil < 0, so :258 counts it overdue and :257 excludes it from due-in-7. Same helper verbatim at AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:157-158 and CompanyProfilePage.tsx:218-219.

CONFIRM: Confirmed. due_date is a Postgres `date` returned as 'YYYY-MM-DD'; `new Date('2026-09-13')` is parsed as UTC midnight (05:30 IST), so NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:250 daysUntil goes negative from 05:30 IST on the due day, counting it as Over Due (:258) and excluding it from 7 Days Due (:257). Identical helpers at AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:157-158 and CompanyProfilePage.tsx:218-219. The calendar (:299-300) is unaffected in IST because getMonth/getDate are local and 05:30 IST is the same day. Fix (string compare against a local YYYY-MM-DD today) is sound; note NoticeWorkflowListView's parseDateLoose parses DD/MM/YYYY locally, so after the fix tile and list will agree.

confirmed_broken.title: 'Failed Logins' tile can never count a failed login, and its drill-down (Company List) uses a different failure definition
confirmed_broken.evidence: failedLoginsCount counts client_sync_log rows with `.eq('action','notices')` (lines 177-181) and status 'failed'. But logSyncAttempt is only ever called from the notices step after login succeeded (content.js:196, 2472, 2732, 2745), and the login handler gives up silently after 3 CAPTCHA bounces: `if (/services\/login/.test(location.href) && $('#captcha') && tries < 3) { job.captchaRetry = tries + 1; ... }` (content.js:503-509) — no log row on exhaustion or on a wrong password. Meanwhile CompanyListPage.tsx:107 loads client_sync_log with NO action filter, and content.js:2739 writes an extra `logClientSync(cur.clientId, 'notices_gstr3a_debug', realFailures ? 'failed' : 'success', …)` AFTER the success row, so on Company List that newer debug row becomes the client's 'latest' status.
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Reproduction 1: change a client's portal password so login fails — the tile stays 0 forever. Reproduction 2: a client whose GSTR-3A PDF rebuild fails shows Status = Failed on /notices-company-list?status=failed (with a 'DNR rules…' message) while the dashboard tile that links there says 0 — the comment at NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:133-139 promising the tile matches the list is false.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: In content.js log a 'failed' client_sync_log row ('Login failed after 3 CAPTCHA attempts' / 'Invalid credentials') when the login retry loop exhausts or an error banner is detected; add `.eq('action','notices')` to CompanyListPage's query (or store the gstr3a debug under a non-'notices' table); rename the tile 'Failed Syncs' unless real login detection is added.

reasons: CONFIRM: logSyncAttempt (content.js:306-309) is the only writer of action='notices' and is called solely inside handleNotices (196 bounce handler when job.step==='notices', 2472, 2732, 2745) — i.e. after login already succeeded. The login handler's CAPTCHA retry (503-509) silently stops when tries >= 3 with no log write, and no wrong-credential detection exists in the login step (the errBanner check at 1545 belongs to the upload flow). Meanwhile CompanyListPage.tsx:107 selects client_sync_log with no action filter and 145-149 takes the newest row per client, while content.js:2739 writes 'notices_gstr3a_debug' AFTER the success row (and 2928/3010/3110 write refunds_debug/refund_docs_debug rows) — so the Company List's latest status can be a debug row while the dashboard tile (filtered to action='notices' at NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:180) reports something else. The comment at :133-139 promising parity is false.

CONFIRM: Confirmed with one correction. logSyncAttempt (content.js:306-309) is only called from the notices step (:196, :2472, :2732, :2745), all after login succeeded. The login handler (:503-509) increments job.captchaRetry up to 3 and then simply does nothing — the job sits on the login page with no client_sync_log row; a wrong password is never detected (`grep -n 'Invalid|Login failed' content.js` finds nothing relevant), and background.js has no watchdog that logs a failure. So the tile (NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:177-181 `.eq('action','notices')`, :264 status==='failed') can only ever count post-login pull failures. CompanyListPage.tsx:107 loads client_sync_log with no action filter, and content.js:2739 writes `logClientSync(cur.clientId, 'notices_gstr3a_debug', realFailures ? 'failed' : 'success', …)` directly via GSTKdb (bypassing the job.logSync guard) after the success row, so that newer row becomes the client's latest on Company List. Correction: the status is 'failed' only when a message does NOT start with 'DNR rules'/'DNR debug call failed' (:2738), so a DNR-only message yields 'success', not 'Failed' — the mismatch appears for real GSTR-3A rebuild failures. Fix is sound; adding `.eq('action','notices')` to CompanyListPage is the minimal safe change.

confirmed_broken.title: KPI tiles and Notice Summary use different definitions of a notice, so Total/Open never reconcile
confirmed_broken.evidence: totalNotices = displayRows.length counts every gst_notices row including 'Refunds'/'Voluntary Payment' case rows and duplicate rows for the same case, whereas computeNoticeSummary (noticeSummaryReport.ts:85) skips those two types and folds them into Refund/DRC 03 rows deduped by ARN/case_id plus rows from gst_refund_applications/gst_drc03_filings that are not in gst_notices at all. Duplicate case rows arise because the extension dedupes task rows only by refId — `if (refId && seenRefs.has(refId)) continue;` (content.js:2607) — so two task rows for one ARN (or rows with null refId) each become a gst_notices row with the same case_id (noticeSummaryReport.ts:69-73 and AllClientsRefundsPage.tsx:73-77 record that 49 raw 'Refunds' rows contain duplicates).
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Reproduction: add up the Notice Summary 'Total' column and compare with the 'Total Notices' tile on the same screen — they differ; likewise 'Open Notices' vs the sum of the Open column. A principal cannot answer 'how many open matters do we have' with one number from this page.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Create one canonical case set (a SQL view v_notice_cases or a shared TS builder) that: excludes PULL FAILED marker rows, collapses gst_notices rows by (client_id, coalesce(case_id, reference_number)), and unions dedicated refund/DRC-03 rows by ARN; drive tiles, summary, calendar and every drill-down from it. Also dedupe task rows by t.arn in content.js.

reasons: CONFIRM: NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:252 `totalNotices = displayRows.length` and :256 openNotices count every gst_notices row, while computeNoticeSummary (noticeSummaryReport.ts:85) skips notice_type 'Refunds'/'Voluntary Payment' and mergeIntoCategory (100-122) unions them with dedicated-table rows by ARN, plus adds dedicated rows not in gst_notices at all. content.js:2607 dedupes task rows only by refId (`if (refId && seenRefs.has(refId)) continue;`) so null-refId rows for one ARN each become a row; AllClientsRefundsPage.tsx:73-77 comment confirms 'the 49 raw case rows include further duplicates'. The tile and the summary Total therefore use different definitions and cannot reconcile.

CONFIRM: Confirmed. NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:252 `totalNotices = displayRows.length` and :256 openNotices count every source='notices' row, including notice_type 'Refunds'/'Voluntary Payment' case rows (written by content.js:2609-2614 with notice_type = titleCase(caseTypeName)) and PULL FAILED markers, while computeNoticeSummary (:85) skips those two types and mergeIntoCategory (:100-122) unions them with the dedicated tables by ARN. The page header comment (:5-10) even states the tiles do not count Refund/DRC-03 while the summary does — a known, but still unreconcilable, divergence. The duplicate-case claim is supported: content.js:2607 dedupes only by refId, and AllClientsRefundsPage.tsx:73-77 records that the 49 raw case rows contain duplicates. Fix (single canonical case set) is sound but is a larger refactor; dedupe by t.arn in content.js must not drop distinct documents that legitimately share an ARN (a case can have several refIds), so key on coalesce(refId, arn) rather than arn alone.

confirmed_broken.title: fetchAllRows pages without ORDER BY and swallows errors, returning partial data as if complete
confirmed_broken.evidence: const { data, error } = await query.range(from, from + PAGE_SIZE - 1); if (error || !data) break;  — no `.order()` is applied by fetchAllRows or by its callers (NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:146-150, AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:124-130, NoticeSummaryReportPage.tsx:52), and an error on page 2 simply stops the loop and returns page 1 as the full result with no signal to the caller.
confirmed_broken.why_it_matters: Postgres offers no stable row order for LIMIT/OFFSET without ORDER BY; a Sync All running while the dashboard loads (delete + insert of a client's rows between page 1 and page 2, background.js:103-104) shifts the offsets so rows are duplicated or skipped, and the tiles show a wrong total with no error. A network/RLS error on page 2 renders a confidently wrong 1000.
confirmed_broken.proposed_fix: Append `.order('id', { ascending: true })` (or created_at,id) inside fetchAllRows before `.range()`, and either throw on error or return `{ rows, error }` so callers can toast and show a retry state instead of a silent partial count.

reasons: CONFIRM: fetchAllRows.ts:20-27: `build(supabase.from(table).select(select))` then `.range(from, from+999)`; `if (error || !data) break;` returns whatever was accumulated. No .order() is applied inside, and none of the three callers add one (NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:149, AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:129, NoticeSummaryReportPage.tsx:52 all pass only `.eq('source','notices')`). AllClientsNoticesPage sorts after the fact (:135) which does not fix offset instability across a concurrent delete/insert from background.js:103-104.

CONFIRM: Confirmed. fetchAllRows.ts:21-23 builds `supabase.from(table).select(select)` and calls `.range()` with no `.order()`, and `if (error || !data) break;` returns whatever was accumulated. None of the callers add an order (NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:146-150, AllClientsNoticesPage.tsx:124-130 sorts client-side afterwards). Postgres gives no stable order for OFFSET pagination without ORDER BY, and Sync All's delete+insert (background.js:103-104) can shift offsets between pages. Fix is sound: appending `.order('id')` inside fetchAllRows after build() is compatible with every caller (they all re-sort or aggregate), and surfacing the error lets finding 13 be addressed.

confirmed_broken.title: Company Dashboard lists and counts each refund/DRC-03 case twice

CONFIRM: Confirmed. CompanyProfilePage.tsx:193 `const combined = [...gstNoticeRows, ...refundRows, ...drc03Rows]` with no dedupe; gstNoticeRows is every source='notices' row for the client (:137), which per content.js:2609-2614 includes 'Refunds'/'Voluntary Payment' case rows with case_id = t.arn, and refundRows/drc03Rows (:159-192) are synthesized with case_id = arn.
