risks: Migration on a live, un-ledgered database: there is no supabase_migrations ledger, so each migration must be applied by hand to gcquafqxbykxkbexcdpy (never SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF) and verified by checking the objects exist; mitigate with idempotent DDL (IF NOT EXISTS), a pre-migration pg_dump of the litigation tables, and PITR enabled in Phase 0 rather than Phase 5 if the plan allows.

Duplicate cleanup before unique indexes: the live data has 0 duplicate (client_id, reference_number) pairs but 55 legitimate multi-task (client_id, case_id) pairs; the case-row partial index must include notice_type or a portal item id or the index creation will fail or collapse real rows - test the index on a copy first.

Stage derivation is an elected position: deriving Open/Closed from ORDRS/CLOSR folder items and status vocabularies will drop 'open' DRC-03 from 167 to ~36 and refunds from 41 to ~19; if the principal disagrees with the rule the numbers swing again. Every rule is tagged CONFIRM-WITH-FIRM in the positions doc and signed off before Phase 3 exposes it on the dashboard.

Extension roll-out is manual: the extension is side-loaded on each staff PC and does not auto-update; old builds still call the delete-then-insert path. The RPCs must tolerate old callers (keep replaceNotices working but routed to the upsert server-side via a compatibility RPC) and the app must refuse Sync All below MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION.

Making return-pdfs private breaks every stored public URL at once (734 notice PDFs, 879 folder attachments, FilingStatus PDFs); the prefix-strip migration and the signed-URL helper must ship in the same release, with a fallback that treats a full URL as a path.

Email volume and trust: a ladder across 473 'overdue' rows would send hundreds of emails on day one; the reminder functions start only after Phase 1's stage derivation reduces the actionable set, with overdue_max = 5, digest-first roll-out for the first week, and a dry-run mode that writes email_outbox rows with status 'preview'.

Microsoft Graph limits: inline attachments over 3 MB fail; large notice PDFs fall back to an app link; Graph throttling on digest mornings is handled by the existing retry/status columns in email_outbox.

Security work touches login: the app_sessions token and server-side role restore change AuthContext; a bug here locks everyone out. Roll out behind a feature flag with the old path available for one release, and test all four roles on staging first.

No test runner today: vitest is introduced in Phase 0 and only covers pure functions; UI regressions are still caught by hand, so each phase ends with a scripted manual checklist run on gst.vjdesai.com by a GST team member.

Scope creep in Phase 4: the litigation module is the largest phase; if capacity slips, E4.3 (MIS/statement) and reply drafting can move to a Phase 4b without affecting the dashboard or emails, because both ride on the Phase 1 model.

Open RLS remains the accepted design (auth.uid() is NULL): even after Phases 0/1/5, any anon-key holder can read the litigation tables. The residual risk is documented in the positions doc as an accepted-risk register entry; sensitive writes and deletes move behind token-validated RPCs, and credentials leave the anon-readable row.
CAPTCHA/ToS legal position for unattended sync is undecided; E5.3 must not enable any solver until the principal records the decision.
kpis_to_track: Data integrity: count of staff-edited columns lost per sync (target 0; measured by comparing non-null staff_status/assigned_to/reply_date before and after each sync_runs row).
Sentinel rows in data tables (target 0 at all times; alert if > 0).
Reconciliation: dashboard Needs-action tile = queue count = Notice Summary open total = GSTIN-wise total (target: zero variance, checked by a nightly SQL assertion that emails on mismatch).
Actionable open matters and Overdue actionable matters (expected to fall from 1060/473 to the true workload after Phase 1; trend weekly).
Median days from notice.new to first_viewed_at (target < 1 working day) and to first reply filed.
Missed statutory deadlines (deadline due_on passed with is_met = false and stage not closed) per month (target 0).
Notice-to-email latency: time from notice.new event to email_outbox status sent (target < 15 min; < 1 min via extension callback).
Email reliability: outbox rows in status failed per week (target < 1%), duplicate sends (target 0 - unique dedupe_key violations logged).
Digest engagement: opens/clicks are not tracked by Graph, so proxy with 'items in yesterday's digest that changed stage within 48 h' (target rising).
Assignment coverage: share of actionable matters with assigned_to set (target > 95%) and unassigned older than 2 working days (target 0).
Sync freshness: clients with credentials whose last successful sync is older than 7 days (target < 5%), and sync_runs completion rate (target > 95% of started runs finish).
Data completeness: share of case matters with a due date, share of DRC-03 rows with amounts, share of refunds with sanctioned amount when an RFD-05/06 exists (targets > 90%).
Demand under dispute ₹, paid ₹ and sanctioned-not-disbursed ₹ tracked monthly for the partner summary.
Security: unauthenticated PDF fetch success rate (target 0), credential reveals per week (audited), anon-key DELETE attempts blocked.
Quality gates: npm run build and npm test green on every merge; vitest fixture updated with an explicit before/after table whenever a KPI definition changes.

best_ideas_to_keep: Phase 0 as a hard gate: upsert_portal_notices/refunds/drc03/case_folder RPCs replacing extension/background.js:102-130 delete-then-insert, deleting the five PULL FAILED writes in content.js (195, 2471, 2744, 2894, 3160), and MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION gating Sync All so a stale side-loaded build cannot keep wiping staff columns.
Portal-owns-portal-columns / staff-own-staff-columns principle, with origin='manual' rows never touched and portal_missing_at soft-missing instead of delete.

Never write diagnostics into data tables: client_sync_log gets run_id, level ('outcome'|'debug'), rows_seen/new/gone, extension_version, actor - and a sync_runs table drives the dashboard health strip.

Security blockers closed before the first email carries a link: manifest host fix, appbridge origin check, inject.js nonce, return-pdfs private + prefix-strip + /notices/:id/pdf signed-URL route, role restored from user_roles not the localStorage blob, StaffRoute wrapper, GSTPortalLink sessionStorage write removed with view_portal_credentials + credential_access_log.

One definition of a notice/due date/closed: src/utils/noticeDates.ts (effectiveDueDate, local-date compare, isActionable) consumed by all four pages, v_notice_cases SQL view with a TS twin, explicit refund/DRC-03 status -> state lookup replacing regexes, and a vitest fixture that asserts the OLD 1060/3/64/92/1060/0/473/0 as it.todo then the NEW numbers so partner-facing figures only change deliberately.

Assignment as a real FK (assigned_to_user_id -> profiles) inside Phase 1 (E1.3), so the T-7/T-3/T-1/T0 ladder reaches a named person from the first email phase, with clients.notice_handler_user_id as default owner and unassigned > first_response_hours escalation to gst_manager.

The fullest email matrix: notice.new with PDF attached, due ladder, overdue repeat with overdue_max, hearing T-3/T-1/T0, order_received with 'appeal by order_date + 3 months', refund deficiency/RFD-08/rejection, sync.failed per client per day, daily digest 08:30 IST Mon-Sat that skips when empty, partner weekly summary, staff-vetted client intimation, backup.failed, nightly sync summary - every one with a deterministic dedupe_key.

Dashboard target layout: six actionable tiles (Needs action / Overdue / Due 7d / Unassigned / High priority / Demand under dispute), action queue with tabs and inline owner select, category card with placeholders collapsed, ageing/issued-vs-closed/workload charts, clients-needing-attention replacing the recent-clients card, 7-day agenda with Month toggle and dot markers, all from one notice_dashboard_stats RPC.

Litigation core modelled correctly for a CA practice: gst_demand_lines per matter x stage x FY x act x head, matter_payments with pre_deposit_s107/s112 kinds and 'Pre-deposit paid' badge, matter_recovery_actions (DRC-13/16/22/22A) with deemed_s107_7 stay, risk_class Possible/Probable/Remote and a contingent-liability schedule report, gst_matter_deadlines with appeal_condonable_limit and rectification_s161.

Phase 4 durability: gst_litigation_history with Restore mirroring the 2B version list, retention_until + legal_hold (s.36), DELETE split out of FOR ALL policies, client soft delete with impact counts, docs/BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY.md with PITR and a quarterly drill.

Positions document with KEEP / CONFIRM-WITH-FIRM / REPLACE tags plus staff SOP and failure runbook, and the CAPTCHA decision (remove fastcaptcha.org host permission until approved) recorded before any unattended sync.
weaknesses: Phase 0 is over-packed: five epics, ~15 person-days including four upsert RPCs, an extension write-path rewrite, folder due-date lifting, job-lifecycle changes, storage lockdown, an edge function, and a positions doc in two weeks; E0.1 at 5 pd is optimistic for one developer.

Phase 2's 'Limitation expiring <= 30 d' and 'Hearings this week' tiles reference gst_matter_deadlines / gst_hearings that only exist in Phase 3 (E3.2); until then only the single hearing_date column added in E0.3 exists, so the target layout is not fully buildable at week 8.

Statutory limitation dates (appeal s.107, GSTAT s.112, s.161, RFD-08, DRC-22A) arrive only in Phase 3 around week 11-14; for a litigation partner the deadline engine is later than it needs to be given that the folder JSON already holds order dates.

No dry-run / preview mode for the reminder ladder: the first 09:00 IST run over today's 473 'overdue' rows (many of which are closed or informational) could flood gst@vjdesai.com before the redefinition of Overdue has been signed off; the risks section only says 'start with the daily digest'.
Phase 3 at 6 weeks / ~33 pd is the largest block and the draft itself concedes it should be split; the roadmap does not actually split it.

Old extension builds are handled only by version gating in the app; there is no server-side compatibility shim, so a PC that still posts to /rest/v1/gst_notices with DELETE keeps working destructively until every PC is reloaded (RLS is open per CLAUDE.md).
Total effort (~110 pd across 18 weeks) still assumes one developer at full pace with the principal available weekly for sign-offs; no slack is budgeted.

best_ideas_to_keep: 'Start from the morning, not the schema': design anchored on what lands in gst@vjdesai.com at 08:30 IST and what a staff member does with it in under a minute - the right framing for the principal's ask.

Route /notices/:id shipped in Phase 1 (E1.3) landing on /notices-all?ref=<reference_number> pre-filtered until the drawer exists in Phase 2, so every email deep link works from day one and never needs to change.

Explicit acknowledgement that the due ladder goes to team_emails until the assigned_to FK lands, with cc gst_manager from T-1 and partners once overdue - honest about the interim rather than pretending assignee routing exists.
Vitest baseline-then-new-definition fixture and a docs/sql/notices_smoke.sql release check asserting no sentinel rows, no duplicate portal keys, tiles = drill-down counts.

gst_extract_folder_dates() SQL function plus a one-off UPDATE lifting due_date for case rows from the latest NOTCE/INTIM/NOTAC item without a later REPLY - makes '7 Days Due' meaningful before any redesign.

Email-fatigue mitigation spelled out: batch notice.new per client per run, cap overdue repeats, respect quiet hours, hand the principal the firm_alert_settings card before enabling the ladder, digest-only for the first week.
Risk note on unique-index cleanup: keep the refund/DRC-03 row that has documents/pdf_url rather than min(created_at) blindly, and the case-row partial index only where reference_number IS NULL.

Refund/DRC-03 first-class model (E4.1): cash/credit split per head, refund_reason_labels table fixing the EXPWP/EXPWOP -> Cash/ITC mapping, v_refund_drc03_cases with a single derived case_state, RFD-08 15-day and s.54(1) two-year re-file deadlines seeded.

Client-facing communication done carefully: staff-vetted intimation with document checklist, gst_matter_communications auto-logged from the outbox, /my-notices read-only view hiding amount/remarks/assignee, opt-in monthly statement, 'awaiting client docs for N days' in the digest.
Precedent library with extracted PDF text and a tsvector index, versioned .docx reply drafts via the existing docx dependency, and 'Mark filed' refused until an approved reply_draft exists.

Reminders of the legal-position risk: the limitation rules in litigationLimitation.ts are the firm's professional positions and must be partner-reviewed and test-pinned with section references and confirmation dates.
weaknesses: Phase 0 is budgeted at 22 person-days for a two-week phase (E0.1 6 + E0.2 6 + E0.3 6 + E0.4 4) - roughly double the available capacity of one developer; the whole plan (~155 pd over 20 weeks / ~100 working days) is over-committed by about half, which the draft half-admits ('roughly 145 person-days').

Named assignee (assigned_to FK) arrives only in Phase 2 (week 6-9), so for the whole first email phase no reminder can reach a specific person - weaker than fix-first, which puts the FK inside the email phase.

Refund and DRC-03 rupee figures, typed columns and the Rs 6.46 Cr / Rs 7.72 Cr backfill wait until Phase 4 (week ~17); the Notice Summary DRC 03 / Refund rows are corrected earlier by the closure vocabulary, but exposure per client on refunds is late for a partner.
Statutory deadline engine and hearings table are Phase 3 (week 10-13); nothing tracks an appeal limitation before then.

Two overlapping note tables (gst_notice_notes in Phase 2 E2.2, then matter-scoped notes in Phase 3) and a hearing marker colour scheme ('warning = hearing') that conflicts with fix-first/platform-first's purple - minor but signals the layout was not reconciled across phases.

Retention/legal hold, credential encryption, DELETE-policy split and backups all sit in Phase 5 (week 18-20); for a litigation system holding evidence that is late, and a client delete still cascades through every litigation table until then.
Weekly client 'docs_reminder' becomes automatic after the first vetted send - a mild breach of its own 'human before client' principle unless the per-client opt-in is enforced.

best_ideas_to_keep: Statutory deadlines seeded during the Phase 1 backfill (gst_seed_statutory_deadlines over every backfilled matter: appeal_limitation order + 3 months, condonable + 4 months, s.161 + 6 months, GSTAT + 3 months, RFD-08 + 15 days, REG-21 90 days, DRC-22A 7 days) - the earliest any draft puts limitation dates into the system (week ~6).

Dry-run mode for the reminder functions that writes email_outbox rows with status 'preview', plus starting the ladder only after stage derivation has shrunk the actionable set from 473 - the strongest guard against a day-one email flood.

Server-side compatibility shim: keep the old replaceNotices REST path working but route it to the upsert via a compatibility RPC, so a stale side-loaded extension cannot wipe staff data even before every PC is reloaded.
Enable PITR in Phase 0 rather than Phase 5 and take a pg_dump of the litigation tables before every hand-applied migration on the un-ledgered gcquafqxbykxkbexcdpy project.
Case-row partial unique index includes coalesce(notice_type,'') to survive the 55 legitimate multi-task (client_id, case_id) pairs, and the risk register says to test the index on a copy first.
Nightly SQL assertion that emails on tile/summary/GSTIN-wise mismatch (KPI 'zero variance, checked by a nightly SQL assertion').
Pre-deposit calculator (10% s.107(6) / 20% s.112(8)) with 'Pre-deposit paid' badge, and an amnesty_128a_eligible generated column (s.73 matters for FY 2017-18..2019-20).

Repointing all existing readers (dashboard, AllClientsNoticesPage, NoticeSummaryReportPage, GstinWiseNoticeCountPage, CompanyProfilePage, refunds/DRC-03 pages, noticeRefundDrc03Reports.ts) at the canonical views so the old pages show corrected numbers before the redesign ships.

Events-drive-everything: emit_gst_notice_event() triggers on gst_notices/gst_matters/gst_hearings/gst_matter_deadlines/refunds/drc03/client_sync_log so the bell, activity feed, 'new since last sync' and emails are all consumers of one stream.
Per-staff subscribable .ics feed (ical_feed_tokens) and a feature-flagged rollout of the app_sessions token change so a login bug cannot lock the firm out.
Extension credentials_status / credentials_checked_at on clients so repeated login failures flag credential problems on the Company List.
weaknesses: Slowest to deliver what the principal asked for: the first team email lands around week 9 (Phase 2 after a 4-week model phase) and the first redesigned screen around week 13; the partner's 'email the GST team on every important matter' waits a month longer than in the other two drafts.

Phase 1 is a big-bang schema drop (gst_matters, stage history, deadlines, hearings, demand lines, notes, counsels, fees, tax_authorities, documents, activity, history, events, communications, notifications - 15+ tables plus 7 RPCs and views) applied by hand to a live database with no migration ledger, before any user-visible payoff; if the backfill heuristics or the principal's sign-off on derived stages stall, everything downstream slips.
Phase 0 is budgeted at 24 person-days for two weeks (E0.1 9 + E0.2 6 + E0.3 6 + E0.4 3) - the most over-committed opening phase of the three.
Extends authenticate_staff to mint app_sessions tokens in Phase 0 (E0.2) - touching the login RPC in the very first sprint carries lock-out risk the draft itself flags but still schedules first.

Drops 'Failed Logins' / GSTIN count into a header subtitle and health strip - correct - but the interim dashboard (weeks 3-13) is only the old page with repointed numbers and quick fixes; no interim action queue.

Assignment as a FK, permission keys, notice drawer and list-view workflow all wait for Phase 3 (week 10-13); staff cannot own or work a notice from the app until then even though emails start at week 9.

WhatsApp, PWA/push and typed IT/TDS capture are explicitly deferred with no phase, and reply drafting/MIS are named as the first things to cut - fine, but it makes the 21-week plan longer than the others while delivering the same end state.

judges.recommended_merge:
Use fix-first as the spine: its phase order (stabilise -> email the team -> rebuild the dashboard around 'what needs attention today' -> litigation core -> durability/credentials/unattended sync) matches how a litigation partner experiences risk, it is the only draft that puts the assigned_to FK inside the email phase so the ladder reaches a named person from week 5, its email matrix and litigation schema are the most complete, and every finding it cites was verified in the code (background.js:102-105, content.js:148/195-214, NoticesDashboardPage.tsx:254, gst_reminders.sql:45-47, send-gst-email/index.ts:5, manifest.json:10/32). Make four corrections to the spine before grafting: (1) stretch Phase 0 to 3 weeks and move E0.5 (vitest/positions doc) to run in parallel with E0.3 rather than after it - 15 pd in two weeks with one developer is not credible; (2) split Phase 3 into 3a (matters + deadlines + hearings) and 3b (demand ledger + documents + MIS/approvals) as its own risks section suggests; (3) fix the internal sequencing bug where Phase 2's 'Limitation <= 30 d' and 'Hearings this week' tiles read tables that only exist in Phase 3; (4) budget one week of slack per phase.

Graft from platform-first: (a) pull a minimal gst_matter_deadlines table and gst_seed_statutory_deadlines() forward into Phase 1 - seeded from order_date/folder ORDRS items and RFD-08 issue dates on the existing gst_notices rows, no matters required yet - so appeal s.107 / GSTAT s.112 / s.161 / RFD-08 / DRC-22A limitation reminders fire in Phase 1 and the Phase 2 tiles have a real source; the full matter linkage happens in Phase 3a. (b) The 'preview' dry-run status on email_outbox and the rule that the ladder only switches on after the Overdue redefinition is signed off (digest-only in week one). (c) The compatibility RPC that routes old extension replaceNotices calls into the upsert, alongside fix-first's MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION gate. (d) Enable PITR and pre-migration pg_dump in Phase 0, not Phase 4. (e) coalesce(notice_type,'') in the case-row partial unique index and the 'test the index on a copy first' step. (f) The nightly SQL reconciliation assertion that emails on tile/summary/GSTIN-wise variance. (g) Pre-deposit calculator and amnesty_128a_eligible generated column into Phase 3b. (h) Repoint the existing pages at v_notice_cases in Phase 0 E0.3 (fix-first already lists this partially) so numbers are right on the old screens before the redesign.

Graft from user-first: (a) Ship route /notices/:id in Phase 1 landing on /notices-all?ref=... until the drawer exists, so no email link ever changes. (b) The docs/sql/notices_smoke.sql release check and the baseline-then-new-definition vitest fixture wording. (c) The email-fatigue rules: batch notice.new per client per run, quiet hours, firm_alert_settings card in the principal's hands before the ladder is enabled. (d) The refund/DRC-03 detail from E4.1 - refund_reason_labels table, cash/credit split per head, s.54(1) re-file limitation and RFD-08 due seeded into deadlines - merged into fix-first's E2.5 so rupee exposure on refunds lands in Phase 2 not later. (e) The unique-index cleanup rule to keep the row with documents/pdf_url rather than min(created_at). (f) Precedent library with extracted-text tsvector search and 'Mark filed refused until approved reply_draft' in Phase 4. (g) The explicit note that litigationLimitation.ts encodes the firm's professional positions and must be partner-reviewed with section references and confirmation dates in the positions doc. Drop from the merged plan: user-first's automatic weekly client docs reminder (keep it staff-vetted every time), and platform-first's Phase 0 change to authenticate_staff (do the app_sessions token in Phase 2 E2.4 behind a feature flag as fix-first schedules).

best_ideas_to_keep: Phase 0 E0.1 is the most complete write-path fix: upsert RPCs that touch only portal-owned columns, portal_missing_at soft-miss, 'refuse to mark-missing when payload is empty', case-task dedupe by t.arn, lifting due_date from NOTCE/INTIM duedt, and the one-off DELETE of 'PULL FAILED%' rows — all mapped to verified lines (background.js:102-105, content.js:195/2471/2744/2894/3160, content.js:148).

E0.1 job-lifecycle items: idle-based expiry replacing the startedAt 20-minute cap (content.js:148), login-failure detection writing client_sync_log action='login', top-level catch → advance(), MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION + extension_version in client_sync_log, actor {userId,name} in every __gstk* postMessage. These make the 'Sync failures' number real.

E0.3 canonical case set (v_notice_cases + TS twin) and the explicit refund/DRC-03 status→state lookup replacing regexes, done BEFORE any email ladder, so the ladder runs over the reduced actionable set rather than 473 rows.
E0.3 fetchAllRows fix (add .order('id') before .range() and return {rows,error}) — matches the real file src/lib/fetchAllRows.ts which breaks silently on error and has no ORDER BY.

E0.5 vitest fixture that asserts the OLD numbers (1060/3/64/92/1060/0/473/0; Refund 60/41/19; DRC 03 183/167/16) as it.todo, then the NEW definitions — the cleanest way to make partner-facing number changes deliberate.

E1.1/E1.2 email plumbing is precisely targeted at the real schema blockers (email_outbox.client_id NOT NULL, kind CHECK at 20260805120000_builder_cancellations.sql:226, send-gst-email/index.ts:86 selecting only to_email, 'No attachments' at line 5) and reuses the vault anon-key http_post cron pattern and the gstReminders immediate-invoke pattern (src/lib/gstReminders.ts:107).
Full event → recipient → template → schedule → dedupe_key matrix for 11 team events plus staff-vetted client intimation; firm_alert_settings single-row table editable from RemindersPage.

E2.4 permission matrix split (sync_notices, assign_notice, close_notice, delete_notice, view_portal_credentials, export_notices, notify_client) plus SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (update_notice_status, assign_notice, delete_notice, grant_permission) validating an app_sessions token — the first realistic mitigation for open RLS.

E3.2 statutory deadline engine keyed on matter_type + stage + base date with the actual section rules (s.107 3 months + 1 condonable, s.161 6 months, RFD-08 15 d, REG-21 90 d, DRC-22A 7 d) and gst_hearings with adjournment outcomes.

E3.3 demand ledger (matter × document_stage × FY × act × head) with matter_payments kinds (pre_deposit_s107/s112, voluntary s.73(5)/s.74(5)) and recovery actions with deemed-stay status — the contingent-liability schedule a CA firm actually needs.
Phase 4 retention: RESTRICT FKs, gst_litigation_history append-only archive, legal_hold/retention_until (s.36), splitting DELETE out of FOR ALL policies, PITR + nightly dump runbook.
weaknesses: Phase 0 is over-committed: 15 person-days of five epics (upsert RPCs, five security holes, canonical view + eight reader repoints, bug sweep, vitest + positions doc) in 2 weeks; E0.4's 1 pd for eight UI items is not honest.

E0.2's get-return-pdf edge function 'validates the app session (staff user id + token from authenticate_staff)' but authenticate_staff returns no token today and app_sessions is only introduced in Phase 2 E2.4 — a sequencing gap; user-first's client-side createSignedUrl(path,300) needs no new token.

Partial unique index (client_id, source, case_id) WHERE reference_number IS NULL can collapse legitimate multi-task rows on one ARN: content.js:2604-2610 builds task rows with reference_number = t.refId (nullable) and case_id = t.arn, so two null-refId tasks on one case collide; the migration needs a duplicate check on a copy first.

Two stage machines: E2.2 adds gst_notices.stage (received…dropped) and E3.1 adds gst_matters.stage; hearing_date/hearing_mode are added to gst_notices in E0.3 then superseded by gst_hearings in E3.2 — avoidable churn on a live table.
References cron job 'gst-send-email-hourly'; the real job is 'gst-send-outbox-hourly' (20260726130000_gst_email_cron.sql) — cron.alter_job by that name would fail.
Refund/DRC-03 typed columns are added in Phase 0 E0.3 schema_changes but the extension/backfill that populates them lands in Phase 2 E2.5 — empty columns for weeks.
No compatibility path for staff PCs still running the delete-then-insert extension build between the migration and the re-load; relies on MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION gating only.
Total ~108 pd across 18 weeks understates Phase 3 (33 pd for matters, deadlines, demand ledger, documents, MIS, masters, approvals, typed forms).

best_ideas_to_keep: Order of work is driven by the two facts that matter (Sync All wipes staff data; no email may carry a link until the bucket is private), then 'Phase 1 is the inbox, Phase 2 is the screen' — exactly the shape of the principal's ask (emailing every important matter; substantially improved look & feel) with visible value by week 5.
E1.3 route /notices/:id lands in Phase 1 with a fallback to /notices-all?ref=<reference_number> so every email deep link works from the first mail, before the drawer exists.

E1.2 groups notice.new by client per run; risks section prescribes digest-only for week one, batching, overdue_max and quiet hours — the only draft that takes email fatigue across 92 GSTINs seriously.

E0.3 signed URLs via src/lib/signedPdf.ts createSignedUrl(path,300) with the anon key — no new edge function or session token needed, ships in the same release as the prefix-strip UPDATE, with a read-time fallback that treats a full URL as a path.

E0.2 lifts case-folder due dates with a SQL function gst_extract_folder_dates() over raw_json plus a one-off UPDATE on gst_notices for case rows — so '7 Days Due' stops being 0 in Phase 0 without waiting for an extension roll-out.

E0.1 refund/DRC-03 dedupe 'must keep the row with documents/pdf_url, not min(created_at) blindly' — the right call given patchRefundDocument writes documents by (client_id, arn) after the base insert (background.js:117-125).

Risk item: keep old REST endpoints working for one release as no-ops that log 'outdated extension' to client_sync_log and show the update banner — realistic for a side-loaded extension on several staff PCs.

E2.1 StaffSelect component reusing the profiles ⨝ user_roles query already in UserControlPage; assigned_to FK with backfill from lower(trim(assign_to)) = lower(profiles.first_name) (profiles has first_name and email — verified).
E2.2 NoticeDrawer with intent actions (Log reply / Log order / Log hearing / Assign / Close with reason / Notify client / .ics) and first_viewed_at for time-to-awareness KPIs.
E5.3 SQL smoke script (docs/sql/notices_smoke.sql: no sentinel rows, no duplicates, tiles = drill-down counts) run before every release — cheap and effective given no test runner exists.
Honest total (~145 pd over 20 weeks, one developer + weekly principal sign-offs) and an explicit statement that Phases 3–4 can be re-cut per epic.
weaknesses: E1.2 'AFTER UPDATE OF assigned_to (Phase 2 column; trigger created now, fires later)' is invalid Postgres — CREATE TRIGGER … AFTER UPDATE OF <column> fails if the column does not exist; the assigned_to column (or the trigger) must move to the same migration.
Phase 0 is 22 pd in 2 weeks (E0.1 6 + E0.2 6 + E0.3 6 + E0.4 4) — over-committed by roughly a factor of two for one developer.
Same partial unique index (client_id, source, case_id) WHERE reference_number IS NULL as fix-first, with the same collision risk on null-refId task rows sharing an ARN (content.js:2604-2610).

Refund/DRC-03 canonical model, typed columns and the DRC-03 amount backfill from vp.pysum wait until Phase 4 (week 14–17), so the all-clients DRC-03 page keeps showing ₹0 for 130 of 183 rows and Notice Summary keeps DRC 03 open 167 for three months after the redesigned dashboard ships.
Typed manual-entry forms per matter_type are bundled into Phase 5 E5.1 (unattended agent sync) — unrelated work in the decision-gated phase.
SECURITY DEFINER RPC layer for status/assign/delete/grant_permission is deferred to Phase 5 E5.2; until then every new permission key from Phase 2 is client-side only.
Phase 0 E0.1 and platform work do not mention a pre-migration pg_dump/PITR before applying unique indexes and DELETEs by hand to gcquafqxbykxkbexcdpy.

best_ideas_to_keep: Compatibility RPC: 'keep replaceNotices working but routed to the upsert server-side' so a stale side-loaded extension build cannot wipe staff columns after the migration — the safest roll-out idea across all three drafts.

Unique index for case rows includes coalesce(notice_type,'') and the risks section names the 55 legitimate multi-task (client_id, case_id) pairs and says 'test the index on a copy first' — the only draft that engages with the real identity of task rows (content.js:2604-2610).

Migration-safety posture: idempotent DDL, pre-migration pg_dump of the litigation tables, PITR enabled in Phase 0 rather than Phase 5, verify objects exist in information_schema after every hand-applied migration — matches CLAUDE.md's 'no migration ledger' warning.
Single stage machine on gst_matters only (no gst_notices.stage) with staff_status kept in sync by trigger for old readers — avoids the two-stage-machine churn in fix-first.
v_notice_cases with effective_due = min unmet deadline due_on else coalesce(extended_due_date, due_date), so tiles, ladder and digest read one definition once the deadline engine exists.
Email dry-run: reminder functions write email_outbox rows with status 'preview' first; digest-first roll-out; Graph 3 MB inline-attachment limit handled explicitly.
Nightly SQL assertion that Needs-action tile = queue count = Notice Summary open = GSTIN-wise total, emailing on mismatch.

emit_gst_notice_event() trigger design keyed on specific column updates (due_date/extended_due_date, staff_status, assigned_to, pdf_url, portal_missing_at) and send-gst-email inserting gst_matter_communications + email.sent on status='sent'.

Backfill specifics grounded in the live data: hearings from the 35 hearing dates in raw_json, demand lines from dmddtls/pymtdtls/vp.pysum (₹6.46 Cr DRC-03, ₹7.72 Cr sanctioned refunds), assigned_to from profiles.first_name with unmatched names logged.
Feature flag + old path for one release when introducing app_sessions/server-side role restore in AuthContext, tested across all four roles — acknowledges that a bug here locks everyone out.
weaknesses: Sequencing fights the ask: no email leaves until Phase 2 (week 7–9) and the first redesigned screen is Phase 3 (week ~10–13), behind a 4-week Phase 1 that creates ~20 tables and backfills matters — the two things the principal asked for arrive last.

Phase 1's stage derivation changes DRC 03 open 167→~36 and Refund 41→~19 and E1.4 re-points every existing page at the new views, yet the risks say the principal signs off 'before Phase 3 exposes it on the dashboard' — the numbers change on live pages before the gate.

Phase 0 is 24 pd in 2 weeks (E0.1 9 + E0.2 6 + E0.3 6 + E0.4 3); Phase 1 25 pd; the largest hand-applied migrations on a live un-ledgered project happen in the first six weeks with the least product feedback.
E0.2 extends authenticate_staff to return an app_sessions token and changes AuthContext bootstrap in Phase 0 — the highest-blast-radius login change is scheduled in the stabilisation phase.
References cron job 'gst-send-email-hourly'; the live job is 'gst-send-outbox-hourly' (20260726130000_gst_email_cron.sql).

Big-bang gst_documents migration in Phase 1 (moving 734 notice PDFs + 879 folder attachments + refund/DRC-03 docs into litigation-docs) before any staff-facing document feature exists; decision on bucket move deferred to the positions doc.
Assigned owners, drawer and the permission split all wait for Phase 3, so the Phase 2 ladder emails mostly fall back to the team list rather than a person.

Less attention to UX specifics that the audit flagged (Import Company reload, calendar contrast, aria-labels are folded into one E0.3 bullet); hearing_date denormalised onto gst_notices 'for list views' reintroduces the dual-source problem it elsewhere avoids.

judges.recommended_merge:
Use **user-first** as the spine. Its phase order (Phase 0 stabilise + security prerequisites → Phase 1 the 08:30 inbox → Phase 2 the screen + owners → Phase 3 litigation core → Phase 4 refunds/MIS/client → Phase 5 keep-it-running) is the only one that delivers both halves of the principal's ask (every important matter emailed to the GST team; substantially improved look & feel) inside the first nine weeks, its per-epic estimates are the most honest (~145 pd / 20 weeks, explicitly re-cuttable), it keeps the deep-link route working from the first email via the /notices-all?ref= fallback, it uses client-side createSignedUrl instead of inventing a session token that authenticate_staff does not return, and it is the only draft that plans the email roll-out for fatigue (digest-first week, per-client batching, overdue_max, quiet hours).

Graft from **fix-first**:
1. Phase 0 E0.1 job-lifecycle items in full — idle-based expiry replacing content.js:148, login-failure detection writing client_sync_log action='login' then advance(), top-level catch → advance(), MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION + extension_version and actor {userId,name} in every __gstk* postMessage, `refuse to mark-missing when payload is empty`. user-first has most of these but fix-first's item list is the implementable spec.
2. Pull fix-first E2.5 / E0.3's refund & DRC-03 typed columns AND the vp.pysum / RFD-05/06 backfill forward into user-first Phase 2 (not Phase 4): ₹0 on 130 of 183 DRC-03 rows and DRC 03 open 167 are visible defects the redesigned dashboard must not inherit for three months.
3. Fix-first E2.4's SECURITY DEFINER RPC layer (update_notice_status, assign_notice, delete_notice, grant_permission validating an app_sessions token) moves into user-first Phase 2 E2.1 alongside the new permission keys, so the keys are enforced server-side from day one instead of Phase 5.
4. Fix-first E0.5's vitest fixture pattern (assert the OLD numbers as it.todo, then the NEW) and the notice_handler_user_id default owner set by upsert_portal_notices.
5. Fix-first E3.2/E3.3 detail (deadline kinds with section references, matter_payments kinds, matter_recovery_actions with deemed_s107_7) as the spec for user-first Phase 3 E3.2/E3.3.

Graft from **platform-first**:
1. The compatibility RPC: keep replaceNotices/replaceRefundApplications/replaceDrc03Filings callable but route them to the upsert server-side, so a stale side-loaded extension build cannot wipe staff columns between the migration and the re-load; combine with user-first's 'outdated extension' log row and banner.
2. Case-row unique key: do NOT ship (client_id, source, case_id) WHERE reference_number IS NULL as written in fix-first/user-first; content.js:2604-2610 sets reference_number = t.refId (nullable) and case_id = t.arn, so null-refId tasks on one ARN collide. Use platform-first's key including notice_type (better: a portal task/item id captured from taskList), run the duplicate check on a copy of gcquafqxbykxkbexcdpy first, and take a pg_dump + enable PITR in Phase 0 before any DELETE or unique index is applied by hand.
3. One stage machine only (gst_matters.stage with staff_status synced by trigger); drop user-first/fix-first's interim gst_notices.stage and hearing_date columns to avoid churn on the live table.
4. Email dry-run (status='preview' rows) and the nightly SQL assertion that tile = queue = summary = GSTIN-wise totals, alongside user-first's release smoke script.
5. v_notice_cases effective_due = min unmet deadline else coalesce(extended_due_date, due_date) once Phase 3 lands, so the ladder and tiles converge on one definition.

Corrections to apply regardless of draft: the outbox backstop cron is 'gst-send-outbox-hourly' (20260726130000_gst_email_cron.sql), not 'gst-send-email-hourly'; user-first's 'trigger created now, fires later' on assigned_to is invalid — the column and the AFTER UPDATE OF trigger must land in the same migration; every Phase 0 estimate (15–24 pd in 2 weeks across the three drafts) should be re-cut to 3 weeks or split so E0.1 (upsert + sentinels) and the bucket lock-down ship first, with the positions doc and canonical view following in week 3.
